title.rendered: Magic Mouse Gestures Guide: How to Use Them on Mac

content.rendered:
Most users treat the Magic Mouse like a regular mouse and only use click, scroll, and right-click. In reality, the entire top surface is touch-sensitive and supports built-in macOS gestures that control navigation, multitasking, and zooming.

With simple taps and swipes, you can switch apps, move between pages, zoom into content, and manage desktop spaces without relying on toolbar buttons or keyboard shortcuts. This guide explains every Magic Mouse gesture, how each one works, and how to adjust them for better efficiency.

Table of Contents
  • Magic Mouse Gestures Overview
  • 1. Left-Click on Magic Mouse
  • 2. Right-Click (Secondary Click)
  • 3. Scroll with One Finger
  • 4. Smart Zoom
  • 5. Swipe Between Pages
  • 6. Open Mission Control
  • 7. Swipe Between Full-Screen Apps and Desktops
  • Customizing Magic Mouse Gestures on Mac
  • Magic Mouse vs Magic Trackpad
  • Conclusion: Getting the Most Out of Magic Mouse Gestures

Magic Mouse Gestures Overview

1. Left-Click on Magic Mouse

The Magic Mouse uses a single touch-sensitive surface instead of separate physical buttons. The top shell detects finger position and pressure to determine which click to register.

To left-click, press on the upper-left area of the surface. macOS reads the position of your finger and registers it as a primary click. Because the surface is unified, avoid resting a second finger on the right side while clicking, as that can trigger a secondary click instead.

Primary click is used for selecting files, opening apps, placing the cursor in text fields, dragging items, and interacting with interface elements across macOS.

2. Right-Click (Secondary Click)

Right-click works using the same surface logic as left-click, but on the opposite side.

To right-click, press on the upper-right area of the surface. The system detects pressure on the right zone and registers it as a secondary click.

If secondary click does not work, enable it in System Settings → Mouse → Point & Click by turning on Secondary Click. You can also choose whether the left or right side activates it, which is useful for left-handed users.

Secondary click opens contextual menus. It is required for renaming files, accessing file options, copying and pasting, saving images, inspecting elements in browsers, and revealing advanced app settings.

3. Scroll with One Finger

Instead of using a mechanical scroll wheel, the Magic Mouse supports full-surface touch scrolling.

To scroll, slide one finger up or down across the surface. The movement is smooth and momentum-based. A slow glide allows precise movement through content, while a quick flick scrolls rapidly through long pages. You can move the finger side by side to scroll horizontally. 

macOS uses Natural Scrolling, meaning content moves in the same direction as your finger. You can disable this in System Settings → Mouse if you prefer traditional scrolling behavior.

Scrolling works system-wide across web pages, long documents, PDFs, Finder windows, spreadsheets, and system menus.

4. Smart Zoom

Smart Zoom provides quick magnification without using zoom controls or keyboard shortcuts.

To activate Smart Zoom, double-tap with one finger. The Mac zooms into the exact area under your pointer. Double-tap again to return to normal view.

Smart Zoom works in Safari, most web browsers, PDFs, and image previews. It is useful for reading small text or inspecting details without changing the overall zoom level of the page.

5. Swipe Between Pages

The Magic Mouse supports horizontal navigation within compatible apps.

Swipe left with one finger to go back. Swipe right with one finger to go forward.

This works in Safari, Chrome, and other browsers, as well as apps that support page-based navigation. It reduces pointer movement and speeds up browsing.

6. Open Mission Control

Mission Control provides an overview of all open windows and desktop spaces.

To open Mission Control, double-tap with two fingers. The screen zooms out and displays every open window, along with desktop spaces and full-screen apps at the top.

From this view, you can switch apps, move windows between desktops, create new desktop spaces, or close windows.

7. Swipe Between Full-Screen Apps and Desktops

When an app enters full-screen mode, macOS places it in a separate desktop space.

To switch between spaces, swipe left or right with two fingers. This moves you horizontally between your main desktop, additional desktops, and full-screen applications.

This gesture allows fast workspace switching without minimizing windows or using keyboard shortcuts.

Customizing Magic Mouse Gestures on Mac

All gestures work by default, but you can adjust behavior to match your workflow.

Open System Settings and click Mouse in the sidebar. From there, you can:

  1. Turn individual gestures on or off.
  2. Disable page swiping if triggered accidentally.
  3. Enable or disable Smart Zoom.
  4. Change scroll direction between Natural and traditional.
  5. Adjust tracking speed.
  6. Adjust double-click speed.

If a specific gesture causes issues, disable only that setting instead of turning everything off. For example, if page swipes are accidentally triggered in Mail or Safari (which can happen often when you want to scroll horizontally), turn off page swipes while keeping Mission Control and Smart Zoom enabled.

Tracking speed affects how far your hand moves across the desk. Faster speeds reduce movement, while slower speeds improve precision for editing or design work. Small adjustments can significantly improve comfort and efficiency.

Magic Mouse vs Magic Trackpad

The Magic Mouse supports essential gestures such as scrolling, Smart Zoom, page swipes, Mission Control, and switching between desktop spaces, while maintaining precise cursor control.

The Magic Trackpad supports all of those gestures plus additional multi-finger controls like pinch to zoom, three- and four-finger app switching, App Exposé, Launchpad access, and Force Click.

Also Check: Magic Trackpad vs Magic Mouse

Use the Magic Mouse if you prioritize cursor accuracy. Use the Magic Trackpad if you rely on advanced multi-finger gestures and faster workspace navigation.

Conclusion: Getting the Most Out of Magic Mouse Gestures

The Magic Mouse combines traditional pointer control with essential macOS gestures in a single touch surface. When you use only click and scroll, you miss the built-in navigation and multitasking shortcuts.

Using page swipes, Smart Zoom, Mission Control, and desktop switching reduces repetitive pointer movement and reliance on the keyboard. With consistent use, these gestures make macOS navigation faster and more efficient. After all, this is unique aspect where Magic Mouse excels above any third-party mouses.

title.rendered: How to Turn On Voice Isolation on iPhone and Improve Call Quality

content.rendered:
Clear audio is not always guaranteed during calls or recordings. Background sounds like traffic, nearby conversations, or even a running fan can quickly make your voice harder to hear, leading to repeated sentences and disrupted conversations. To solve this, Apple introduced Voice Isolation on iPhone, a feature designed to reduce surrounding noise and keep your voice clear during calls and recordings.

Here’s everything you need to know about Voice Isolation on iPhone and how to enable it.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Voice Isolation on iPhone?
  • Which iPhones and iPads Support Voice Isolation?
  • Which Apps Support Voice Isolation on iPhone?
  • Voice Isolation Requirements: iOS Version and Device Compatibility
  • How to Enable and Use Voice Isolation on iPhone and iPad
  • When Should You Use Voice Isolation on iPhone?
  • Does Voice Isolation Turn On Automatically on iPhone?
  • Summing Up

What Is Voice Isolation on iPhone?

Voice Isolation is an iPhone audio feature that makes your voice clearer during calls and recordings by reducing background noise. It works by prioritizing speech and filtering out ambient sounds such as wind, traffic, or nearby conversations.

The option appears only when an app is actively using your iPhone’s microphone, such as during phone calls, FaceTime, supported third-party calling apps, or voice recording apps. Once enabled, Voice Isolation keeps your voice in focus so the person on the other end hears you more clearly, even in noisy environments.

Which iPhones and iPads Support Voice Isolation?

Voice Isolation is supported on the following devices:

  • iPhone XR, iPhone XS models and later
  • iPad (8th generation) and later
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M4)
  • All iPad Pro 11-inch models
  • iPad Pro 12.9-inch (3rd generation) and later
  • iPad Air (3rd generation) and later
  • iPad mini (5th generation) and later

Which Apps Support Voice Isolation on iPhone?

Voice Isolation works on iPhones running recent versions of iOS and is supported in:

  • Phone calls
  • FaceTime audio and video calls
  • WhatsApp, Zoom, and other VoIP apps (app support may vary)
  • Voice Memos and third-party recording apps that access the microphone

The feature activates per app session, meaning you can enable it separately depending on where you are making the call.

Voice Isolation Requirements: iOS Version and Device Compatibility

Before using Voice Isolation, make sure your iPhone is running a compatible iOS version. Feature availability varies depending on how you are using the microphone.

  • FaceTime calls and supported third-party apps: Requires iOS 15 or later
  • Audio or video recording apps (such as Voice Memos): Requires iOS 26 or later
  • Phone calls: Requires iOS 16.4 or later

How to Enable and Use Voice Isolation on iPhone and iPad

Voice Isolation can only be turned on while an app is actively using your iPhone’s microphone. The option appears in Control Center during a call or recording session, which is why you will not see it in Settings beforehand.

Here’s how to enable it on an iPhone or iPad:

  1. Start a call or recording, then swipe down from the top right corner of your screen to open Control Center.
  2. Tap [App] Controls at the top center.
  3. Select Voice Isolation under Audio & Video.
  4. Close Control Center and continue your call or recording.

Once enabled, background noise will decrease, and the person on the other end of the call will hear you more clearly.

If Voice Isolation feels too aggressive in certain situations, you can choose from other microphone modes.

  • Automatic: Requires iOS 18 or later. This mode selects the best microphone setting for your situation. For example, it may use Voice Isolation for receiver calls and Standard for speakerphone. If your environment has high background noise, your iPhone may automatically prioritize your voice.
  • Standard: Standard mode does not alter audio processing. It transmits your voice as it is.
  • Wide Spectrum: Wide Spectrum captures a broader range of audio during your call. This can be useful if you want background sounds, such as live music during a video call, to be heard clearly.

Voice Isolation works independently for each app. Enabling it during a Phone or FaceTime call does not automatically apply the setting to other calling apps.

When Should You Use Voice Isolation on iPhone?

Voice Isolation is especially useful when background noise could interfere with communication, such as:

  • Taking calls in crowded places
  • Working from cafés or public spaces
  • Outdoor conversations with traffic noise
  • Online meetings and professional calls
  • Recording voice notes in noisy environments

Does Voice Isolation Turn On Automatically on iPhone?

No. Voice Isolation does not turn on by itself. You must enable it manually from Control Center during a call or recording.

If your iPhone is set to Automatic Mic Mode, the system manages microphone processing automatically, but this is different from Voice Isolation. Automatic mode dynamically adjusts audio, while Voice Isolation specifically reduces background noise and prioritizes your voice.

Once enabled, Voice Isolation remains active for that app until you change the microphone mode again.

Summing Up

Voice Isolation is one of the most useful yet underrated iPhone features for improving call quality. By filtering background noise and prioritizing your voice, it makes conversations clearer without requiring additional apps or accessories. Once you know where to find it in Control Center, enabling it takes only a few seconds and can noticeably improve how others hear you.

Did Voice Isolation improve your call quality? Share your experience in the comments below.

FAQs

Why is Voice Isolation not working on my iPhone?

If Voice Isolation is not working, check your iOS version and make sure you enabled it during an active call or recording session. You can also review troubleshooting steps in a dedicated fix guide.

Where is Voice Isolation on my iPhone?

The Voice Isolation option appears in Control Center while you are on a call or using an app that accesses the microphone.

Does Voice Isolation consume extra battery?

The effect Voice Isolation has on your iPhone’s battery life is negligible.

Does Voice Isolation work if the other person is using an Android phone?

Yes. As long as you enable Voice Isolation on your iPhone, it will improve how your voice is transmitted, regardless of the device the other person is using.

How do I disable Voice Isolation?

Swipe down to open Control Center, select Mic Mode, and choose Standard or Automatic.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Apple’s Merge function keeps the highest-quality file and combines the metadata. The discarded copies are moved to Recently Deleted, where they remain for 30 days before being permanently removed.

mainEntity.name: Will Deleting Duplicate Photos Free Up iCloud Storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If iCloud Photos is turned on, deleting duplicate photos and videos using the built-in Duplicates feature will free up iCloud storage space.

mainEntity.name: Will Third-Party Apps Offer Better Duplicate Detection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Apple detects only exact duplicates. Third-party apps can also identify: Live Photo variations Similar photos Screenshots Blurry shots These apps provide more advanced detection options for deeper cleanup.

keyPoints.title: Voice Isolation suppresses background noise during calls
keyPoints.explanation: This feature isolates your voice from surrounding sounds, making your speech clearer on the other end.

keyPoints.title: Availability of Voice Isolation on iOS 16 and later
keyPoints.explanation: You can use Voice Isolation on iPhone devices running iOS 16 or newer, ensuring compatibility with recent models.

keyPoints.title: How to enable Voice Isolation on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Access the Control Center during a call, select Controls, and tap on Voice Isolation to activate it for clearer communication.

keyPoints.title: Supported devices for Voice Isolation
keyPoints.explanation: Voice Isolation works on iPhone XR and newer, various iPad models, including iPad Air, mini, and all iPad Pro 11-inch models.

keyPoints.title: Tips for using Voice Isolation effectively
keyPoints.explanation: Use the feature with built-in or external microphones, and be aware that nearby voices may sound amplified when noise suppression is active.

title.rendered: How to Use Dynamic Island on iPhone: Complete Guide

content.rendered:
Dynamic Island transforms the once static notch into a live, adaptive display that keeps your most important alerts, activities, and app updates right at your fingertips. Think of it as a smart companion built directly into the top of your screen. This guide explains what Dynamic Island is, how it works, its standout features, and practical ways to use it in everyday life.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Dynamic Island on iPhone?
  • Key Features of Dynamic Island on iPhone
  • How to Use Dynamic Island on iPhone
    • Basic Interactions
    • Practical Ways to Use Dynamic Island in Everyday Life
  • Tips to Use Dynamic Island More Efficiently
  • Dynamic Island vs Live Activities: What's the Difference?
    • What Are Live Activities?
    • How Live Activities Work With Dynamic Island
  • Pros and Cons of Dynamic Island on iPhone
  • Wrapping Up

What Is Dynamic Island on iPhone?

Dynamic Island is the pill-shaped area at the top of the iPhone screen that houses the front camera and Face ID sensors. It replaces the older static notch with a flexible space that grows, shrinks, and animates depending on what is happening on your iPhone.

Apple introduced this feature with the iPhone 14 Pro lineup and now includes it across the latest iPhone models. It works as a live status hub that keeps ongoing activities, such as timers, calls, navigation, or media playback, visible while you continue using your phone.

Supported devices include:

  • iPhone 14 Pro and 14 Pro Max
  • iPhone 15, 15 Plus, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max
  • iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max

Key Features of Dynamic Island on iPhone

Before diving in, here are the features that make Dynamic Island so useful:

  • Alerts and Notifications: Dynamic Island displays quick alerts such as calls, Apple Pay confirmations, AirDrop transfers, charging updates, and privacy indicators in a compact view.
  • Live Activities: It shows real-time updates from apps, allowing you to follow sports scores, deliveries, rides, and flights without leaving your current app. These updates remain visible in a compact form and expand when you long-press.
  • Background Activities: Dynamic Island makes it easy to monitor ongoing tasks. When you play music, set a timer, start navigation, or record your screen, a small preview remains visible so you can check progress at any time. It also shows connected accessories, such as AirPods or hotspot activity.
  • Split View for Multiple Activities: When two tasks run at the same time, Dynamic Island displays them in two bubbles. For example, you can see music playback on one side and a timer on the other. You can tap either side to expand it or swipe between them for quick control.

How to Use Dynamic Island on iPhone

Here are step-by-step, practical instructions with real examples.

Basic Interactions

Dynamic Island responds to simple gestures so you can check or control tasks quickly.

Practical Ways to Use Dynamic Island in Everyday Life

Dynamic Island is most helpful when it shows information you would normally switch apps to check. Many third-party apps also support it for quick updates.

  • Music and Podcasts: When you play a song in Apple Music, YouTube Music, Spotify, or another app, Dynamic Island shows track details and a waveform. Long-press to pause, skip, or change audio output without opening the app.
  • Timers and Countdowns: Start a timer and glance at the top of your screen to see the countdown. Tap to return to the Clock app or long-press to pause or cancel it.
  • Navigation: Apple Maps or Google Maps displays turn-by-turn directions in the Island. You can see your next turn and distance while using other apps. A long-press reveals more details.
  • Ride Updates: Apps like Uber and Lyft show your driver’s ETA and trip progress so you can keep browsing or messaging without switching back.
  • Delivery Tracking: Food and package delivery apps update arrival times in Dynamic Island. This keeps you informed without reopening the app.
  • Screen Recording: When recording your screen, a red indicator and timer appear in the Island. Tap it to stop recording quickly.
  • Flashlight Indicator: Turning on the flashlight shows an indicator in Dynamic Island. On supported models, you can adjust brightness or beam width with simple swipe gestures.
  • Parking Timer Reminders: If you use a parking timer app, the remaining time stays visible at the top of your screen so you can check it at a glance.

If you want to dismiss an activity, simply swipe it to the side.

Other popular examples include:

  • Live sports and score updates such as ESPN or MLB
  • Health and fitness apps like SmartGym, Posture Pal, Steps
  • Productivity and finance tools like Dynamic Island Notes & Memo or Calzy
  • Weather apps such as Carrot Weather
  • Games like Hit The Island
  • Cooking apps such as Pestle

Tips to Use Dynamic Island More Efficiently

Make Dynamic Island cleaner and faster to use with these tips:

  • Use apps that support Live Activities for richer real-time updates.
  • Adjust Live Activities in Settings to control what appears and reduce clutter.
  • Use long-press gestures for quick actions instead of opening full apps.
  • Keep your iPhone updated for improved animations and app support.
  • Limit unnecessary background activities.
  • Allow notifications only from apps you want visible in the Island.

Dynamic Island vs Live Activities: What’s the Difference?

Dynamic Island turns the notch area into a functional hub. It makes important updates easier to follow and keeps ongoing tasks within reach.

What Are Live Activities?

Live Activities are real-time notifications that stay visible on your Lock Screen and in Dynamic Island on supported iPhones. They show continuously updating information such as:

  • Sports scores
  • Food delivery progress
  • Ride‑share arrival time
  • Timer countdowns
  • Music playback info
  • Flight status

Apps update these Live Activities in the background so you can glance at them without reopening the app.

How Live Activities Work With Dynamic Island

Dynamic Island acts as the interactive space where Live Activities appear. They show as compact indicators that you can expand for more details or controls. The Island can handle multiple activities at once with smooth transitions.

In simple terms, Live Activities provide the data, and Dynamic Island provides the interface.

Related: Live Activities on Apple Watch: How to Use and Customize Them

Pros and Cons of Dynamic Island on iPhone

Pros

  • Provides real-time updates without interrupting your workflow.
  • Helps you multitask by keeping active apps visible at the top of the screen.
  • Offers quick access to essential controls through long-press gestures.
  • Displays smooth animations that make alerts easy to understand.
  • Works automatically with supported apps, requiring no setup.

Cons

  • Can feel distracting when multiple activities appear at once.
  • Does not allow customization of its appearance or behavior.
  • Depends on developer support, so not all apps work with it yet.
  • Split view can feel cramped when two activities are shown.
  • Animations may occasionally pull attention away from your main task.

Wrapping Up

Dynamic Island blends design and usability in a practical way. It keeps important updates visible and makes multitasking easier. Once you get comfortable with the gestures, it becomes a natural part of using your iPhone every day.

FAQs

Does Dynamic Island drain the battery?

It uses a small amount of power, but the impact is minimal because it updates only when something changes.

Can you disable Dynamic Island?

No. It cannot be turned off completely. However, you can reduce how often it appears by limiting Live Activities and notifications.

Can apps customize icons on the Island?

Yes. Apps can display their own icons and activity cards, but they must follow Apple’s design guidelines. Developers cannot change the Island’s shape or system animations.

  • Download iPhone 15 and 15 Pro wallpapers in 4k (Free)
  • iPhone 15 vs. iPhone 14 – What are the differences?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Apple’s Merge function keeps the highest-quality file and combines the metadata. The discarded copies are moved to Recently Deleted, where they remain for 30 days before being permanently removed.

mainEntity.name: Will Deleting Duplicate Photos Free Up iCloud Storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If iCloud Photos is turned on, deleting duplicate photos and videos using the built-in Duplicates feature will free up iCloud storage space.

mainEntity.name: Can you disable Dynamic Island?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It cannot be turned off completely. However, you can reduce how often it appears by limiting Live Activities and notifications.

title.rendered: How to Rename Photos, Videos, and Files on iPhone and iPad

content.rendered:
Giving your photos, videos, and files meaningful names on your iPhone or iPad makes them easier to organize, quicker to find, and more professional when shared. However, renaming files in iOS and iPadOS does not always work the same way it does on a Mac or Windows PC. Some apps allow you to change the actual file name, while others only let you label or organize items within the app.

Keep reading to learn which iPhone apps support true file renaming and the correct ways to rename photos, videos, and documents on iPhone and iPad.

Table of Contents
  • Why Renaming Photos, Videos, and Files Works Differently on iPhone and iPad
  • How to Rename Photos and Videos on iPhone and iPad
  • How to Rename Files on iPhone and iPad
    • Rename Files Using the Files App
    • Rename Documents Using the Pages App
  • Can You Rename Files in the Photos App?
  • Can You Rename Files in the Preview App?
  • Bonus Tip: Add Captions in the Photos App for Easier Searching
  • Renaming Files Made Simple

Why Renaming Photos, Videos, and Files Works Differently on iPhone and iPad

If you have tried renaming a photo inside the Photos app and found no rename option, your iPhone is working exactly as intended.

Unlike the Files app, photos and videos stored in the Photos app are not treated as regular documents that you can freely edit or rename. Instead, Apple designed the Photos app to function as a media library. Images are organized using metadata such as date, location, people, and visual recognition rather than traditional file names.

Because of this design:

  • The Photos app does not provide direct control over file names
  • Renaming options are intentionally unavailable
  • File-level actions are handled outside the Photos library

If you need to change the actual file name, you must first save the photo to the Files app, which provides access to the file system.

That said, Apple does offer a workaround inside Photos through captions. Captions act as searchable labels and help you find images quickly without changing the original file name.

How to Rename Photos and Videos on iPhone and iPad

Since the Photos app does not allow direct file name changes, you need to move the photo or video to the Files app first and then rename it. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Photos app and select the photo or video you want to rename.
  2. Tap the Share button in the bottom left corner.
  3. Scroll down and tap Save to Files.
  4. Choose a folder under On My iPhone or iCloud Drive.
  5. Before saving, tap the file name field at the bottom of the screen.
  6. Enter the new file name and tap Save.

The media will now be saved in the Files app with the new file name.

If you forget to rename the file while saving it, you can rename it later directly inside the Files app. You can also rename attachments received in the Mail app by saving them to the Files app and renaming them there.

How to Rename Files on iPhone and iPad

You can rename documents, PDFs, images, downloads, and other files directly using the Files app. Apple’s Files app works as the central file manager in iOS and iPadOS, giving you full control over file names and folders.

Rename Files Using the Files App

  1. Open the Files app and navigate to the folder containing the file.
  2. Locate the document or file.
  3. Press and hold the file thumbnail.
  4. Tap Rename in the menu that appears.
  5. Enter the new name, then tap the right tick (Done) button to save the changes.

If the file is stored in iCloud Drive, the updated file name syncs automatically across your devices.

Rename Documents Using the Pages App

If you are working with documents created in the Pages app, you can rename them directly within the app:

  1. Open the Pages app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Find the document in the document browser.
  3. Press and hold the document thumbnail.
  4. Tap Rename.
  5. Enter the new name and tap Done.

Can You Rename Files in the Photos App?

No, you cannot truly rename files directly inside the Photos app on iPhone or iPad. The Photos app functions as a media library rather than a file system.

Within Photos, you can:

  • Edit images and videos
  • Add captions for easier searching
  • Organize items into albums and folders
  • Mark favorites or adjust metadata such as location

Can You Rename Files in the Preview App?

The Preview feature on iPhone and iPad allows you to open and edit supported files, but it primarily works as a viewer and markup tool rather than a file manager. You cannot rename media or documents directly in Preview. Its functionality is limited to viewing, annotating, signing, and editing content.

Bonus Tip: Add Captions in the Photos App for Easier Searching

While you cannot rename photos directly in the Photos app, you can add captions to make them easier to find later. Captions act as searchable labels and are indexed by both the Photos app and Spotlight search.

Here’s how to add a caption:

  1. Open the Photos app and select the photo or video.
  2. Tap the i (Information) button at the bottom of the screen.
  3. Tap the Add a Caption field.
  4. Enter a name, keyword, or short description.
  5. Tap Done to save your changes.

Renaming Files Made Simple

That’s how you rename photos, videos, and files on your iPhone and iPad. The Files app remains the central place for full file name control, while apps like Pages provide limited document management. Apps such as Photos and Preview are designed primarily for viewing and editing rather than file management.

If you have questions about renaming files on your iPhone or have discovered another useful tip, feel free to share your experience in the comments.

  • How to Organize Photos on Mac Like a Pro
  • How to delete Documents and Data on iPhone and iPad

mainEntity.name: Is It Safe to Merge Duplicate Photos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Apple’s Merge function keeps the highest-quality file and combines the metadata. The discarded copies are moved to Recently Deleted, where they remain for 30 days before being permanently removed.

mainEntity.name: Will Deleting Duplicate Photos Free Up iCloud Storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If iCloud Photos is turned on, deleting duplicate photos and videos using the built-in Duplicates feature will free up iCloud storage space.

mainEntity.name: Will Third-Party Apps Offer Better Duplicate Detection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Apple detects only exact duplicates. Third-party apps can also identify: Live Photo variations Similar photos Screenshots Blurry shots These apps provide more advanced detection options for deeper cleanup.

acceptedAnswer.text: If Voice Isolation is not working, check your iOS version and make sure you enabled it during an active call or recording session. You can also review troubleshooting steps in a dedicated fix guide.

mainEntity.name: Where is Voice Isolation on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Voice Isolation option appears in Control Center while you are on a call or using an app that accesses the microphone.

mainEntity.name: Does Voice Isolation consume extra battery?

acceptedAnswer.text: The effect Voice Isolation has on your iPhone's battery life is negligible.

mainEntity.name: Does Voice Isolation work if the other person is using an Android phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. As long as you enable Voice Isolation on your iPhone, it will improve how your voice is transmitted, regardless of the device the other person is using.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Snapchat Launches Creator Subscriptions to Offer Exclusive Paid Content

content.rendered:
Snapchat has announced Creator Subscriptions, a new monetization feature that allows users to pay for exclusive content from their favorite creators. The company confirmed that the feature will begin testing in an alpha phase with a limited group of creators in the United States starting February 23.

The new offering aims to give creators a recurring revenue stream while enabling closer engagement with their most dedicated followers.

What Creator Subscriptions Offer

According to Snap’s official newsroom announcement, users will be able to subscribe to creators directly within the Snapchat app. Subscribers will gain access to several exclusive perks, including:

  • Subscriber-only Stories and Snaps
  • Priority replies from creators to subscribers
  • An ad-free viewing experience for that creator’s Stories

Creators will also have control over their monthly subscription pricing, though Snapchat plans to recommend pricing tiers to help guide creators during setup.

Expanding Monetization Options for Creators

Snapchat says Creator Subscriptions are designed to complement its existing creator monetization ecosystem rather than replace it. The company already operates programs such as the Unified Monetization Program and Snap Star Collab Studio, which focus on ad revenue sharing and brand partnerships.

With subscriptions, creators can generate recurring income directly from fans instead of relying solely on advertising revenue or one-time collaborations.

In its blog post, Snap explained that the feature is intended to strengthen creator-fan relationships by offering more direct interaction and exclusive content experiences.

Related: How to Tell If Someone Has Snapchat Plus

Gradual Rollout Planned

For now, Creator Subscriptions will remain limited to select creators in the U.S. during the testing phase. Snapchat plans to expand availability to Snap Stars in Canada, the United Kingdom, and France in the coming weeks before rolling out the feature more broadly.

The company added that access will expand gradually across creators, users, and devices as testing continues.

Would you subscribe to your favorite Snapchat creator? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

Also read:

  • How to Fix Snapchat Login Issues

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Apple’s Merge function keeps the highest-quality file and combines the metadata. The discarded copies are moved to Recently Deleted, where they remain for 30 days before being permanently removed.

mainEntity.name: Will Deleting Duplicate Photos Free Up iCloud Storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If iCloud Photos is turned on, deleting duplicate photos and videos using the built-in Duplicates feature will free up iCloud storage space.

title.rendered: iOS 26.4 Adds CarPlay Support for ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini

content.rendered:
Apple is expanding CarPlay’s app capabilities with iOS 26.4. For the first time, third-party AI chatbots will be allowed to run directly within the CarPlay interface, bringing voice-based conversational apps like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini into the car.

The change is outlined in Apple’s updated CarPlay Developer Guide and is currently available in the iOS 26.4 beta. A public release is expected this spring.

CarPlay Now Supports Voice-Based Conversational Apps

Starting with iOS 26.4, Apple is introducing a new supported app category: voice-based conversational apps. This allows developers of AI chatbot services to build dedicated CarPlay integrations.

Previously, CarPlay supported only a limited set of app types such as navigation, audio, messaging, and EV charging. AI chatbot companies were effectively locked out, leaving drivers limited to Siri for voice interactions inside the vehicle.

With the update, companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google can add CarPlay compatibility to their iPhone apps, provided they adopt Apple’s new framework and entitlement for conversational apps.

A New Voice Control Screen Designed for In-Car Use

Apple is introducing a dedicated voice control screen for these apps. When a supported chatbot is active, CarPlay will display a vehicle-optimized interface that provides visual feedback during conversations.

Developers must implement this voice control screen to gain approval. Apple is also requiring a specific entitlement for voice-based conversational apps, reinforcing its long-standing approach of tightly controlling which app experiences are allowed on CarPlay.

The interface is designed to minimize distraction. It focuses on voice interaction rather than complex on-screen controls.

No Vehicle Controls and No Wake Word Support

Despite the deeper integration, third-party AI apps will have limitations.

They will not be able to control vehicle functions or iPhone system features. In addition, there is no wake word support for these apps. Users must manually open the chatbot app through CarPlay before starting a conversation.

Once launched, the experience is fully hands-free, but activation still requires user input.

This keeps Siri as the default system-level voice assistant, while allowing alternative AI tools for question-answering and conversational tasks.

Rolling Out With iOS 26.4 This Spring

iOS 26.4 is currently in beta testing and is expected to ship publicly this spring. When it does, chatbot developers that update their apps will be able to bring AI conversations into CarPlay for the first time.

The move signals a broader shift in Apple’s approach. Rather than building its own all-encompassing AI assistant for every scenario, Apple is opening parts of its ecosystem to external AI providers, while maintaining tight guardrails around safety and distraction in the car.

excerpt.rendered: Apple is opening CarPlay to third-party AI chatbots in iOS 26.4, introducing a new voice interface while keeping tight control over safety and system access.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Apple’s Merge function keeps the highest-quality file and combines the metadata. The discarded copies are moved to Recently Deleted, where they remain for 30 days before being permanently removed.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If iCloud Photos is turned on, deleting duplicate photos and videos using the built-in Duplicates feature will free up iCloud storage space.

mainEntity.name: Where is Voice Isolation on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Voice Isolation option appears in Control Center while you are on a call or using an app that accesses the microphone.

mainEntity.name: Does Voice Isolation consume extra battery?

title.rendered: How to Restore Apple Watch From a Backup

content.rendered:
So, you’re considering resetting your Apple Watch, maybe to fix a glitch or because you’re switching devices. The big question is: how do you back it up? Since there’s no obvious manual backup button on the watch, many users aren’t sure whether their data is safe. While this can feel confusing, Apple Watch backups happen automatically through your paired iPhone.

This guide explains how Apple Watch backups work, what’s included in a backup, and how to restore your Apple Watch step by step.

Table of Contents
  • Does Apple Watch Automatically Back Up?
  • What Data Gets Restored on Apple Watch (And What Doesn’t)
    • Data That Gets Restored
    • Data That Does NOT Get Restored
  • What to Do Before Restoring Apple Watch From a Backup
  • How to Restore Your Apple Watch From a Backup
  • How to Restore Apple Watch to a New iPhone
  • How to Check if an Apple Watch Backup Exists Before Resetting
  • Apple Watch Not Restoring From Backup? Try These Fixes
  • How Long Does an Apple Watch Restore Take?
  • Can You Restore an Apple Watch Without an iPhone?
  • Back to Normal

Does Apple Watch Automatically Back Up?

Unlike iPhones or iPads, Apple Watch doesn’t have a separate backup system. Instead, backups are created automatically and stored on your paired iPhone.

Here’s how it works:

  • A backup is created when you unpair your Apple Watch from your iPhone.
  • The backup is stored on the paired iPhone, not on the watch itself.
  • When your iPhone backs up to iCloud or a computer, the Apple Watch backup is included within it.

What Data Gets Restored on Apple Watch (And What Doesn’t)

You might assume an Apple Watch backup includes everything on your device, from settings and saved data to paired Bluetooth accessories. In reality, only certain types of data are restored, while some items must be set up again.

Here’s what gets restored and what doesn’t:

Data That Gets Restored

When you restore from a backup, the following typically returns:

  • App data and installed apps
  • Watch face layout and complications
  • System settings and preferences
  • Messages settings
  • Notification settings
  • Health and fitness data if iCloud Health syncing is enabled
  • Accessibility and Dock settings

Data That Does NOT Get Restored

You will need to set up some items again:

  • Apple Pay cards
  • Bluetooth device pairings
  • Apple Watch passcode
  • Certain calibration data
  • Some Mail and Messages data, which may sync again afterward and appear gradually

What to Do Before Restoring Apple Watch From a Backup

Before pairing your Apple Watch again to restore it from a backup, make sure:

  • Your iPhone is running the latest available iOS version.
  • Your Apple Watch battery is at least 50 percent.
  • Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are turned on.
  • Both devices remain close together.
  • Your iPhone is signed in with the same Apple ID that was used when you unpaired the Apple Watch.
  • If you’re pairing the Apple Watch with a new iPhone, your previous iPhone’s backup has been restored to it.
  • iCloud Health is enabled if you want health data restored.

If you haven’t yet unpaired your Apple Watch, unpairing it first creates the most recent backup.

How to Restore Your Apple Watch From a Backup

To restore your Apple Watch from a backup, you must first unpair it from the paired iPhone using the Watch app. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Watch app and tap All Watches.
  2. Tap the i button next to your Apple Watch.
  3. Tap Unpair Apple Watch.

This automatically creates a fresh backup.

Once the unpairing process is complete, you can restore the watch using the latest backup or an older one, if available. Follow these steps:

  1. Press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears on the Apple Watch.
  2. Next, bring the Apple Watch close to your iPhone. The pairing pop-up should appear automatically. If it doesn’t, open the Watch app on your iPhone and tap Pair Apple Watch.
  3. Select Set Up for Myself or Set Up for a Family Member based on your need.
  4. Now, position your Apple Watch in the frame to begin the pairing process.
  5. Once pairing is complete, the Watch app will ask if you want to restore from a backup or set up the Apple Watch as new. Select Restore from Backup.
  6. Select the backup you want to restore.
  7. Once done, follow the on-screen instructions to set up your Apple Watch.

After setup finishes, apps and data will continue syncing in the background.

How to Restore Apple Watch to a New iPhone

If you’ve upgraded to a new iPhone, you must first restore it using your previous iPhone’s backup. You can restore from either a local backup on a Mac or Windows PC or from an iCloud backup.

Once that’s complete, follow the steps in the previous section to restore your Apple Watch from the existing backup.

How to Check if an Apple Watch Backup Exists Before Resetting

Apple doesn’t show Apple Watch backups as a separate list, which can make it difficult to confirm whether one exists before resetting your watch. However, because Apple Watch backups are stored within your iPhone backup, an existing iPhone backup also means an Apple Watch backup is available.

Here’s how to check:

  1. Go to Settings → iCloud → iCloud Backup.
  2. Check the date and time of the last successful backup.
  3. If the backup was created recently, your Apple Watch backup is included in it.

Apple Watch Not Restoring From Backup? Try These Fixes

If the restore option doesn’t appear or fails:

  • Update both iPhone and Apple Watch software.
  • Make sure both devices use the same Apple ID.
  • Restart your iPhone and Apple Watch.
  • Restore the iPhone backup first if you’ve switched phones.
  • Keep both devices connected to Wi-Fi during setup.

You like to read: How to Mirror Your Apple Watch on Your iPhone

How Long Does an Apple Watch Restore Take?

There’s no fixed timeline for restoring an Apple Watch backup. The restore time depends on the size of the backup, your internet speed, and how much data needs to sync back to the watch.

In most cases, the initial restore process takes between 10 and 30 minutes. After that, apps, photos, and messages continue syncing in the background.

For the fastest restore experience, keep your Apple Watch and iPhone close together, connected to Wi-Fi, and plugged into a charger. A large app library or extensive health and fitness data may increase the overall syncing time.

Can You Restore an Apple Watch Without an iPhone?

No. You cannot restore an Apple Watch without an iPhone. Apple Watch backups are tied to the paired iPhone, so you must use an iPhone to restore your data. If you don’t have access to the original iPhone backup or you reset the watch directly from the watch itself, it must be set up as new.

Back to Normal

That’s how you restore your Apple Watch from a backup. Unlike the iPhone, restoring an Apple Watch is straightforward because Apple automates most of the process. As long as your iPhone backup exists, pairing the watch again and selecting the correct backup quickly brings back your apps, settings, and familiar layout.

If you’re still facing issues restoring your Apple Watch, let us know in the comments.

FAQs

How often does Apple Watch back up data?

A backup is created automatically whenever the watch is unpaired and whenever the paired iPhone is backed up to iCloud or a computer.

Can I restore to an older Apple Watch model?

Yes, as long as the model supports the required watchOS version and you use the same Apple ID.

Does restoring delete the current Apple Watch data?

Yes. The Apple Watch is erased during setup before a backup can be restored.

title.rendered: How to Mute Yourself or Others on FaceTime

content.rendered:
Ever been on a FaceTime call where someone’s background noise or constant interruptions steal all the attention? It happens to everyone. The good news is that FaceTime gives you simple controls to keep your calls calm and distraction free.

In this guide, you’ll learn how to mute someone in FaceTime using practical workarounds so you can stay focused on the conversation that matters. I’ll also walk you through the steps to mute FaceTime calls and notifications.

  • Can You Mute Someone in FaceTime?

  • Keep Your FaceTime Calls Chaos Free

Can You Mute Someone in FaceTime?

Let’s start with the basics. Unfortunately, FaceTime does not allow you to mute another person directly. Apple designed the app so that each participant controls their own microphone settings.

Here’s what you can do:

  • Mute yourself so others cannot hear you
  • Lower your device volume
  • Use system audio controls
  • Silence incoming calls and notifications

In group FaceTime calls, the app automatically highlights the person who is speaking. However, audio control still depends on each participant managing their own microphone.

How to Mute Yourself in FaceTime on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

Muting yourself in FaceTime is quick and easy once you know where to look.

On iPhone and iPad

  1. During a FaceTime call, tap the screen to show call controls.
  2. Tap the microphone icon.
  3. The icon will show as crossed out, confirming your microphone is off.

Since the iPad uses the same FaceTime interface as the iPhone, the steps are identical. The other person can still see you during a video call, but they will not be able to hear you. They also will not receive any notification that you muted yourself.

If you try to speak while muted, your iPhone will detect your voice and show a prompt indicating that your microphone is off. Simply tap the microphone icon again to unmute.

This works the same way for both video calls and audio only FaceTime calls. It is especially useful during meetings and group calls. If you are in a noisy environment, open Control Center during the call, tap FaceTime, and select Voice Isolation to reduce background noise.

Related: How to Turn On Voice Isolation on iPhone

On Mac

  1. During a FaceTime call on Mac, move your cursor over the FaceTime window.
  2. Click the Mute button (microphone icon).
  3. Click it again to unmute.

If you are using AirPods, headphones, or an external microphone, muting in FaceTime will still control your audio input.

You can also enable Voice Isolation on your Mac to make your voice clearer and minimize background noise.

How to Mute Someone Else on FaceTime on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

If you are in public, it can feel awkward to keep your FaceTime call loud and audible. Since you cannot mute other participants directly, the only true solution is to ask them to turn off their microphone if there is excessive background noise.

If you simply do not want to hear the other person without letting them know, here are your options:

  • Lower the volume using your iPhone or iPad side volume buttons during the call. On a Mac, press the F10 key to mute the output volume.
  • Switch the audio output to AirPods or headphones and set them aside so you no longer hear the call.

In group FaceTime calls, conversations can become noisy when multiple people talk at once. FaceTime helps by automatically focusing on the person who is speaking, but overall audio levels remain under your control.

How to Silence FaceTime Calls on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

Sometimes you do not want to mute audio during an active call. Instead, you may want to silence incoming FaceTime calls or notifications so they do not interrupt your work. Here are a few ways to do that.

Method 1: Mute Incoming Calls

The fastest way to silence FaceTime calls is to use Silent Mode.

On newer iPhones:

  1. Open Settings and tap Sounds & Haptics.
  2. Toggle on Silent Mode.

Older iPhones have a physical mute switch on the side. Flip it to enable Silent Mode.

On iPad, press and hold the Volume Down button to quickly reduce sound output.

To stop FaceTime call sounds on a Mac:

  1. Go to the Apple Menu and select System Settings.
  2. Click Notifications on the left pane, scroll down, and select FaceTime.
  3. Toggle off Play sound for notification.

FaceTime calls will still come through, but they will not make a sound.

Method 2: Use Focus Mode

You can also silence calls using Focus mode, including Do Not Disturb.

On iPhone and iPad:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Focus and select Do Not Disturb.
  3. Select Apps > Silence Notifications From.
  4. Tap Add Apps and choose FaceTime. Hit the checkmark.

Enable the selected Focus mode whenever needed.

This prevents FaceTime calls from ringing while you are busy. You can set up Focus mode on your Mac as well to silence FaceTime calls and notifications during work hours.

Method 3: Silence Unknown Callers

If you want to avoid interruptions from people you do not know, you can enable the Silence Unknown Callers feature for FaceTime. This automatically silences calls from numbers or Apple IDs that are not saved in your contacts.

On iPhone and iPad:

  1. Open Settings and go to Apps.
  2. Scroll down and tap FaceTime.
  3. Toggle on Silence Unknown Callers.

On Mac:

  1. In the FaceTime app, click FaceTime on the menu bar and select Settings.
  2. Click FaceTime.
  3. Look for the Call Filtering section and click the tick box next to Unknown Callers. 

Once enabled, calls from unknown contacts will not ring. Instead, they will go to voicemail and appear under Recents so you can review them later if needed.

Keep Your FaceTime Calls Chaos Free

FaceTime makes video and audio calls simple across Apple devices, and its muting controls help keep conversations clear and distraction free. While you cannot mute another person directly in FaceTime, you can easily mute yourself, manage call audio, and silence incoming calls when necessary.

Now that you know how to mute and silence FaceTime calls, you are in full control of when and how you stay connected.

title.rendered: How to Control F on iPhone to  Find Words Instantly

content.rendered:
Ever wished you could use Control + F on your iPhone like you do on a computer? Good news: you can. While there’s no literal Control key on your iPhone, Apple has built the same functionality right into iOS—it’s just hiding in plain sight.

In this guide, I’ll show you exactly how to use “Control F” on your iPhone to search for specific words or phrases across Safari, Chrome, PDFs, and even Notes.

Table of Contents
  • What Does Control + F Do?
  • Why Use Control + F on iPhone?
  • How to Use Control + F on iPhone in Different Apps
    • How to Use Control F on iPhone in Safari
      • Method 1: Using Reader Mode
      • Method 2: Using the Share Menu
    • How to Use "Control F" in Google Chrome on iPhone
    • Search within a document via Files app
    • Search for words or phrases within Apple Notes

What Does Control + F Do?

Control + F (or Command + F on Mac) helps you quickly find words or phrases in documents, web pages, or PDFs without manually scrolling. On iPhone, this function is just as useful—especially when you’re digging through long articles or dense notes.

Why Use Control + F on iPhone?

Here are common use cases:

  • Scanning long articles in Safari or Chrome.
  • Searching PDFs or eBooks for a term or reference.
  • Finding details inside lengthy Notes or Pages documents.

How to Use Control + F on iPhone in Different Apps

Whether you’re browsing in Safari or Chrome, reading a PDF, or digging through Notes, here’s how to quickly find exactly what you need.

Use Control F in Safari

Safari hides the “Find on Page” tool in a couple of places. Here’s how to access it:

Method 1: Using Reader Mode

  1. Open the Safari webpage where you want to search for a particular word or phrase.
  2. Tap the Reader Mode icon in the address bar.
  3. Tap the Find on Page button at the bottom left corner.
  4. Enter the word or phrase you’re looking for, and the matches will be highlighted instantly.
  5. Use the arrows at the right to move between the matches.

Method 2: Using the Share Menu

  1. Tap the Share button.
  2. Scroll and tap Find on Page.
  3. Type the term and navigate using the arrows.

Bonus tip: You can also type the term directly into the address bar, scroll down, and tap Find “[term]” On This Page from the results.

Use “Control F” in Google Chrome

Chrome offers a similar “Find in Page” feature:

  1. Open the Google Chrome webpage.
  2. Tap the Share button next to the address bar
  3. Select Find in Page.
  4. Type your term and use the arrows to browse matches.

Alternatively, you can tap the three-dot button menu > choose the Find in Page option in the menu that appears.

Search Within a Document via the Files App

PDFs in the Files app come with a built-in search tool:

  1. Go to the Files app and open the PDF document in which you want to look for a particular word or phrase.
  2. Tap the Magnifying Glass (Search) icon.
  3. Enter your search term and use the arrows to switch between results.

Search for Words or Phrases within Apple Notes

Apple Notes makes it effortless to search within a note:

  1. Open the note in the Notes app.
  2. Tap the Three Dot button at the top right corner.
  3. Select Find in Note.
  4. Enter the word or phrase you want to look for, and the matches will be highlighted instantly. Use the arrow buttons to move between the highlighted matches.

Stop Scrolling, Start Searching

The Control + F shortcut isn’t exclusive to computers anymore. Whether you’re researching online, scanning PDFs, or reviewing notes, your iPhone has smart tools to help you find exactly what you need in seconds.

Now that you know how to “Control F” on iPhone, ditch the endless scrolling and jump straight to the info that matters.

Explore more iPhone tips and tricks:

  • How to take a screenshot on an iPhone and iPad
  • How to clear iCloud storage on iPhone and iPad
  • Safari tips and tricks for iPhone

keyPoints.title: Using Control + F on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: iPhone users can now easily search for specific words or phrases within apps like Safari, Chrome, PDFs, and Notes using built-in iOS features that mimic the Control + F functionality on computers.

keyPoints.title: What does Control + F do?
keyPoints.explanation: Control + F (or Command + F on Mac) helps quickly find words or phrases in documents, web pages, or PDFs, and this utility is now available on iPhone for easier navigation through long content.

keyPoints.title: Why use Control + F on iPhone?
keyPoints.explanation: This feature is especially useful for scanning long articles, searching PDFs, or finding specific details within lengthy Notes or Pages documents efficiently.

keyPoints.title: How to use Control + F in Safari and Chrome
keyPoints.explanation: In Safari, you can access 'Find on Page' via Reader Mode or Share menu, while Chrome offers 'Find in Page' through the Share button or the three-dot menu, enabling quick searches within web pages.

keyPoints.title: Searching within PDFs and Notes
keyPoints.explanation: You can search for words or phrases within PDF documents using the Files app's search tool or inside Apple Notes by using the 'Find in Note' feature to highlight matches instantly.

Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Apple Event on March 4: What to Expect From the Apple Experience

content.rendered:
Apple has invited select journalists and creators to attend a “special Apple Experience” scheduled for March 4 in New York, London, and Shanghai. While the company has not confirmed what will be unveiled, new reports suggest Apple may roll out announcements gradually throughout the week rather than hosting a traditional livestream event.

A Week of Announcements Instead of One Event

According to Daring Fireball’s John Gruber, Apple may introduce new products through a series of Newsroom press releases published daily from Monday, March 2, through Wednesday, March 4. The March 4 gathering would serve as a hands-on media experience rather than a keynote.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman supported this theory, saying the staggered announcement schedule aligns with information he has heard from sources familiar with Apple’s plans. Gurman also indicated that Apple is unlikely to host a conventional livestreamed event, though short promotional videos could accompany each product reveal online.

Apple has used this rollout strategy before. Similar multi-day announcement cycles occurred in March 2019 and again in October 2024, when the company introduced multiple Macs through consecutive press releases.

Products Rumored for Early March

Several Apple devices are rumored to be nearing launch, though not all are expected to launch in the same week.

1. Lower-cost MacBook

Apple is reportedly developing a more affordable MacBook powered by an A18 Pro chip. The device may feature a 12.9-inch display and launch in multiple color options.

2. iPhone 17e

The next-generation budget iPhone 17e could include an A19 chip, MagSafe support, and updated Apple wireless chips. Current rumors suggest Apple will keep the notch design, with pricing starting around $599 in the U.S.

3. iPad Air

A routine refresh is expected, upgrading from the M3 chip to the M4 processor for improved performance and efficiency.

4. Entry-level iPad

Apple may update the standard iPad with a jump from the A16 chip to either an A18 or A19 chip.

5. MacBook Air

The MacBook Air lineup is rumored to transition from M4 to M5 chips, focusing on performance gains rather than a major redesign.

6. MacBook Pro

Updated models could feature M5 Pro and M5 Max chips alongside PCIe 5.0 support, enabling faster SSD speeds.

7. Mac Studio

A performance refresh may bring M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, targeting professional workflows and high-end computing tasks.

8. Studio Display

A new version is rumored to include mini-LED backlighting, HDR support, and a refresh rate up to 120Hz, powered by an A19-series chip.

9. Home Hub

Apple’s smart home hub is expected to feature a 6 to 7-inch display, Apple Intelligence support, FaceTime integration, and a redesigned Siri experience.

10. Apple Security Camera

An Apple-designed HomeKit security camera could launch alongside the Home Hub as part of a broader smart home push.

Not Everything May Arrive at Once

Despite the lengthy list of rumored products, analysts expect only a small subset to launch during the first week of March. The most likely candidates currently include:

  • The lower-cost MacBook
  • The iPhone 17e
  • Either a refreshed iPad Air or an entry-level iPad

Rumors surrounding updated Apple TV and HomePod mini models continue to circulate, though recent reports suggest they may not be ready yet.

Clues From the Invite

The “Apple Experience” invite features a colorful Apple logo composed of yellow, green, and blue discs. Gurman previously reported that Apple was testing similar color options, including pink, for the rumored budget MacBook, suggesting the device could play a central role in the event.

With media attending hands-on sessions on March 4, Apple appears to be prioritizing in-person demonstrations while shifting announcements to a press-release format.

More details are likely to emerge as the first week of March approaches.

What are you expecting Apple to announce during the March 4 Apple Experience? Share your predictions in the comments below.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as long as the model supports the required watchOS version and you use the same Apple ID.

mainEntity.name: Does restoring delete the current Apple Watch data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The Apple Watch is erased during setup before a backup can be restored.

title.rendered: Apple Is Developing AI Smart Glasses, AI Pin, and Camera-Equipped AirPods

content.rendered:
Apple is accelerating development of three AI-focused wearable devices: smart glasses, a wearable AI pin, and AirPods with integrated cameras. The effort is part of a broader push to expand Apple Intelligence beyond the iPhone, according to Bloomberg.

All three products are designed to work alongside the iPhone and a more advanced version of Siri currently in development. Each device includes cameras intended to give Apple’s AI systems visual awareness of a user’s surroundings.

Smart Glasses Could Launch in 2027

Apple’s smart glasses are being developed as a competitor to Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses. Internal prototypes have been distributed to hardware teams, with a 2027 launch target. Production could begin as early as December 2026.

The glasses will not feature a display in the lenses. Instead, they rely on voice interaction through Siri.

They are expected to include two cameras: a high-resolution camera capable of capturing photos and video, and a secondary sensor that interprets environmental context and measures distance, similar to LiDAR on the iPhone.

Planned features include voice-controlled phone calls, music playback, photo and video capture, object recognition, walking navigation, and contextual responses based on what the user is looking at. Apple is also exploring capabilities such as reading physical text and adding event details to the calendar, live translation, and context-aware reminders.

Apple has opted to design its own frames rather than partner with an existing eyewear brand. The frames use premium materials, including acrylic elements, and integrate the battery and core components directly into the structure. Multiple sizes and colors are expected at launch.

Also Read: Apple Glasses Take Priority as Apple Cancels Vision Pro Revamp

AI Pin Remains in Early Development

Apple is also developing a wearable AI pin or pendant, though the project remains in early stages and could be canceled. If it proceeds, it could launch in 2027.

The device includes a low-resolution, always-on camera designed to provide environmental context to Siri, but it is not intended for capturing photos or video. A built-in microphone allows voice interaction.

The AI pin is being positioned as an iPhone accessory rather than a standalone device. Most processing will be handled by the iPhone. The pin contains a dedicated chip similar in capability to the one used in AirPods. Apple is still deciding whether to include a speaker for two-way audio responses.

The device could attach to clothing or bags via a clip, or be worn as a pendant using an integrated attachment point.

Camera-Equipped AirPods May Arrive Sooner

AirPods with integrated cameras are further along in development and could launch as early as this year.

Like the AI pin, the cameras are designed for contextual awareness rather than photography. Visual data would be used to enhance Siri’s understanding of the user’s environment.

Upgraded Siri Is Central to the Strategy

All three devices depend on a significantly upgraded Siri experience. Apple is developing a chatbot-style version of Siri for iOS 27 that relies on AI models developed by Google.

Although recent Apple Intelligence features have rolled out gradually, these wearables are being built around a more capable assistant that can process visual input and respond with contextual information.

Broader AI Hardware Roadmap

In addition to these devices, Apple is working on augmented reality glasses with an integrated display, though that product remains several years away.

The company is also developing a home hub smart display expected later this year, along with a larger-screen version featuring a robotic arm that could launch in 2027. A new HomePod and a compact indoor sensor for home security and automation are also in development.

Together, the projects signal Apple’s push to extend AI across wearable and home hardware, with the iPhone continuing to serve as the primary processing hub.

title.rendered: What Is Switch Control on iPhone and iPad and How to Use It

content.rendered:
Apple has long prioritized accessibility, building features into iPhone and iPad that help people interact with their devices in ways that match their physical abilities and personal preferences. Among these tools, Switch Control stands out as one of the most powerful and customizable options. It allows you to operate your iPhone or iPad without relying on traditional touch gestures, using switches, adaptive accessories, or alternative input methods to navigate, select items, and perform actions across the system.

Here is everything you need to know about Switch Control and how to use it.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Switch Control on iPhone and iPad?
  • How Does Switch Control Work?
  • What’s New in Switch Control in iOS 26?
    • 1. Switch sets
    • 2. Slide to Type
    • 3. Move to AssistiveTouch
    • 4. Eye tracking support
  • How to Turn On Switch Control on iPhone and iPad
  • How to Use Switch Control to Navigate Your iPhone or iPad
    • Step 1: Watch as items on the screen are highlighted automatically
    • Step 2: Activate your switch when the desired item is selected
    • Step 3: Use the Switch Control menu to perform actions like:
  • How to Customize Switch Control Settings
    • Change the Scanning Style
    • Adjust Scanning Speed and Timing
    • Change Highlight Appearance
    • Create Custom Gestures
    • Set Up Recipes for Different Tasks
    • Configure Audio Feedback
  • Switch Control vs AssistiveTouch vs Voice Control: What’s the Difference?
  • Final Thoughts

What Is Switch Control on iPhone and iPad?

Switch Control is an accessibility feature on iPhone and iPad that lets users control their device using external switches, screen taps, or adaptive accessories instead of standard touch gestures.

It is primarily designed for people with motor impairments or limited mobility, allowing them to navigate the interface, select items, type, and perform actions using one or more switches. The system works through an automatic scanning interface that highlights items on the screen, which you can select using a switch input.

In simple terms, Switch Control lets you operate your iPhone or iPad with minimal physical interaction.

How Does Switch Control Work?

Switch Control uses a scanning system that automatically highlights selectable items. You interact with the device by triggering actions when the correct item is selected.

There are three scanning styles you can choose from, based on your preference:

  • Auto Scanning: The cursor automatically moves across screen elements at a set speed.
  • Manual Scanning: One switch moves between items while another selects.
  • Single-Switch Step Scanning: One switch controls navigation and selection via timed steps.

A floating menu provides additional actions, such as scrolling, gestures, and system controls.

What’s New in Switch Control in iOS 26?

Recent updates to Switch Control make it faster, smarter, and more flexible, introducing improvements that simplify navigation and reduce setup friction.

1. Switch sets

You can now create multiple switch configurations and switch between them instantly. This allows different setups for different tasks without reconfiguring switches each time.

Example use cases include:

  • One setup for typing
  • Another for browsing or media control

This change removes the need to repeatedly adjust switch assignments.

2. Slide to Type

Typing becomes faster by allowing you to draw a path across the keyboard using the cursor instead of selecting each key individually. The system predicts words based on cursor movement, similar to swipe typing on a touchscreen keyboard.

3. Move to AssistiveTouch

You can now jump directly from Switch Control to AssistiveTouch via the Switch Control menu, making it easier to switch between accessibility tools as needed.

4. Eye tracking support

Eye Tracking lets your gaze control the cursor via the front-facing camera. A switch input confirms selections, enabling near hands-free device navigation.

How to Turn On Switch Control on iPhone and iPad

Enabling and setting up Switch Control on your iPhone and iPad is straightforward and can be completed in a few taps. Here’s how:

  1. Open Settings and head to Accessibility.
  2. Here, select Switch Control under the Physical and Motor section.
  3. Now, toggle Switch Control on, then tap OK to confirm.

Once enabled, scanning begins immediately on the screen.

After enabling Switch Control, you must assign at least one switch before using it. Here’s how:

  1. In the Switch Control settings, tap Switch.
  2. Tap Add New Switch, then select the switch source you prefer.
  3. Now, assign one of the available actions under:
    • Scanner
    • Navigation
    • System

Repeat the process to add multiple switches for more advanced control.

How to Use Switch Control to Navigate Your iPhone or iPad

Once Switch Control is enabled and at least one switch is set up, you can start navigating your iPhone or iPad using scanning and switch actions instead of touch gestures.

Step 1: Watch as items on the screen are highlighted automatically

Switch Control scans the interface by moving a highlight box across buttons, icons, and menus. The highlight moves based on your selected scanning style and timing settings.

Step 2: Activate your switch when the desired item is selected

When the highlight reaches the item you want, trigger your assigned switch. This action selects the item and typically opens the Switch Control menu rather than executing the action immediately.

Step 3: Use the Switch Control menu to perform actions like:

  • Tap to open apps or press buttons
  • Scroll through pages or lists
  • Perform gestures such as swipes or pinches
  • Access device controls like notifications, Control Center, or volume settings

Select an action from the menu using your switch to complete the interaction.

To exit Switch Control, you can either head to Settings → Accessibility → Switch Control or use the Accessibility Shortcut if you have assigned one.

How to Customize Switch Control Settings

After enabling and setting up Switch Control, customizing its settings is the most important step. Proper configuration improves accuracy, reduces accidental selections, and speeds up navigation.

Change the Scanning Style

Scanning determines how items are highlighted on your screen.

  1. In the Switch Control settings, tap Scanning Style.
  2. Here, choose one of the available options: Auto Scanning, Manual Scanning, or Single Switch Step Scanning.

Adjust Scanning Speed and Timing

Timing settings control how responsive Switch Control feels.

  1. Tap Auto Scanning Time.
  2. Now, tap the plus (+) or minus (–) buttons to increase or decrease the scanning speed.
  3. Next, head back and adjust these options:
    • Pause on First Item: Adds a short delay before scanning begins.
    • Loops: Sets how many times scanning repeats across the screen.
    • Move Repeat: Allows repeated actions when holding a switch.
    • Long Press: Assigns secondary actions when holding the switch longer.

Start with slower timing and gradually increase speed once comfortable.

Change Highlight Appearance

Adjusting visual feedback makes scanning easier to follow.

  1. Go to Settings → Accessibility → Switch Control.
  2. Here, scroll to the Visual section and make the following changes:
    • Toggle on Large Cursor to increase the size of the cursor.
    • Tap Cursor Color to choose a different cursor color.

Create Custom Gestures

You can perform complex touch gestures using a switch.

  1. Go to Settings →Accessibility → Switch Control.
  2. Scroll down and tap Saved Gestures.
  3. Tap Create New Gestures.
  4. Perform a gesture on the screen, such as a swipe or a pinch, then tap Save.
  5. Name your gesture, then tap Save to confirm.

Set Up Recipes for Different Tasks

Recipes allow switches to behave differently during specific activities.

  1. In the Switch Control settings, tap Recipes.
  2. Here, tap Create New Recipe.
  3. Enter a name for the recipe.
  4. Tap Assign a Switch.
  5. Next, select the switch you want to customize, then choose the action it should take while this recipe is active.
  6. Now, head back and toggle on Timeout and choose how long the recipe should remain active before Switch Control returns to the default setup.

Configure Audio Feedback

Switch Control can play sounds and provide spoken feedback to help you understand what is being selected during scanning. This is useful if you don’t want to rely only on visual highlights.

  1. Go to Settings →Accessibility → Switch Control.
  2. Scroll down to the Audio section and toggle on Sound Effects.
  3. Next, tap Speech to enable spoken feedback for highlighted items and menu actions.

Switch Control vs AssistiveTouch vs Voice Control: What’s the Difference?

iPhone and iPad offer multiple accessibility tools that help users interact with their devices without relying entirely on standard touch input. While Switch Control, AssistiveTouch, and Voice Control may seem similar at first, each serves a different purpose and is designed for different interaction needs.

Here is how they compare:

Final Thoughts

And that’s it; now that you know that once set up correctly, Switch Control can make everyday device use more accessible, precise, and comfortable. With customizable controls and support for alternative input methods, it provides a flexible way to navigate, type, and interact with the entire system.
