title.rendered: How to Sync Messages Between iPhone and Mac (iMessage, SMS, MMS, RCS)

content.rendered:
Keeping your messages in sync across your iPhone, iPad, and Mac makes communication much easier. You can start a conversation on one device and continue it on another without losing context. Apple handles this through iCloud, which keeps everything updated in the background.

In this guide, you will learn how message syncing works, how to set it up on each device, and how to fix common issues so your messages stay perfectly aligned everywhere.

Table of Contents
  • How Apple Message Syncing Works
  • What You Need Before Syncing Messages
  • How to Enable Messages in iCloud on iPhone and iPad
  • How to Sync Messages Between iPhone and Mac
  • How to Sync SMS, MMS, and RCS Messages on Mac and iPad
  • How to Manage Message History and iCloud Storage
  • Fix Messages Sync Issues Between iPhone, iPad, and Mac
    • Messages Not Appearing on Mac or iPad
    • Sync Stuck or Continuously Updating
    • Fixes for Network and iCloud Errors
  • Final Thoughts

How Apple Message Syncing Works

iMessage works over the internet and syncs automatically across Apple devices. When you send, delete, or receive a message, the change is uploaded to iCloud and then pushed to your other devices. If you set up a new device using the same Apple ID, your message history will appear there as well.

SMS, MMS, and RCS messages rely on your carrier and require Text Message Forwarding to appear on your iPad, Mac, or Apple Vision Pro. This feature is powered by Apple’s Continuity ecosystem.

No matter which method you use, your messages remain end-to-end encrypted. This means even Apple cannot read your conversations, keeping your data private and secure.

What You Need Before Syncing Messages

Before turning on message syncing, make sure everything is set up properly.

  • Apple ID requirements: All devices must be signed in to iCloud using the same Apple Account.
  • Privacy settings: iCloud Keychain and two-factor authentication must be enabled.
  • iCloud storage: Large message histories, photos, and videos use storage, so make sure you have enough free space.
  • Internet connection: Your iPhone must be powered on and connected to Wi-Fi or mobile data.

How to Enable Messages in iCloud on iPhone and iPad

Start with your iPhone, since it typically handles all messaging.

  1. Open Settings and tap your Apple ID name.
  2. Select iCloud.
  3. Tap Messages under Saved to iCloud.
  4. Toggle on Use on this iPhone.

All messages and attachments you send or receive will now be stored in iCloud.

Follow the same steps on your iPad to sync iMessage, SMS, MMS, and RCS messages. Make sure your iPad is signed in with the same Apple ID as your iPhone.

How to Sync Messages Between iPhone and Mac

If you have never used Messages on your Mac, you will need to set up iMessage first. Open the Messages app and sign in with your Apple Account email address and password.

To enable iCloud syncing for Messages on Mac:

  1. Launch the Messages app.
  2. Go to Messages in the menu bar and select Settings.
  3. Open the iMessage tab.
  4. Check Enable Messages in iCloud.
  5. Choose which phone numbers and email addresses you want to use for messaging on your Mac.

All messages sent or received on your Mac will now sync with your other devices. Initial syncing may take several minutes or longer, depending on your message history and internet speed.

How to Sync SMS, MMS, and RCS Messages on Mac and iPad

Messages in iCloud stores iMessages, SMS, MMS, and RCS texts, which can use significant iCloud storage. If you are low on storage or do not want everything synced across all devices, you can use Text Message Forwarding instead.

This lets you choose specific devices to receive text messages without using iCloud. iMessages will still sync normally.

On iPhone:

  1. Go to Settings > Apps > Messages.
  2. Tap Text Message Forwarding.
  3. Toggle on your iPad and Mac.

How to Manage Message History and iCloud Storage

  • Deleting a message on one device removes it everywhere once syncing is complete.
  • You can keep messages Forever, For 1 Year, or For 30 Days. To change this, go to Settings > [Apple ID] > iCloud > Messages and select Keep Messages.
  • To reduce iCloud storage usage, delete large attachments, remove old conversations, or adjust message retention settings.
  • You can also turn off Messages in iCloud without deleting messages already stored locally on your device.

Fix Messages Sync Issues Between iPhone, iPad, and Mac

If messages are not appearing on your iPad or Mac, these are the most common problems and fixes.

1. Messages Not Appearing on Mac or iPad

  • Make sure the same Apple ID is used on all devices. Using multiple Apple IDs is the most common cause of sync issues.
  • Turn Messages in iCloud off and back on for your Mac and iPad.
  • Confirm Text Message Forwarding is enabled on your iPhone.
  • Open Settings > [Apple ID] > iCloud > Messages and Sync Now to ensure the latest messages are uploaded to iCloud.
  • Update all devices to the latest software version.

2. Sync Stuck or Continuously Updating

  • Restart all devices.
  • Make sure your iPhone, iPad, and Mac are connected to the internet.
  • Sign out and back into iCloud. On your iPhone and iPad, go to Settings > Apps > Messages > Send & Receive and tap on your Apple Account > Sign Out. Similarly, you can sign out iMessage on Mac.
  • Check Apple’s iCloud system status.

3. Fixes for Network and iCloud Errors

  • Switch between Wi-Fi and cellular data. A strong connection is required for large message histories.
  • Turn off any active VPN.
  • Reset Network Settings if needed.
  • Verify iCloud services are online using Apple’s System Status page.

Final Thoughts

If you regularly use more than one Apple device, message syncing is well worth enabling. Once everything is set up correctly, your conversations stay available wherever you need them, saving time and keeping your inbox organized.

Now that you know how message syncing works, take a moment to check your settings and enable it if you have not already. If this guide helped, share it with someone who switches between Apple devices and explore more Apple tips to get the most out of your iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

FAQs

Do deleted messages disappear everywhere?

Yes. Once synced, deleted messages are removed from all devices.

Can messages sync without iCloud?

No. iCloud is required for real-time iMessage syncing. Only SMS, MMS, and RCS messages can sync without iCloud using Text Message Forwarding.

What happens if a device is offline?

Messages will sync automatically once the device reconnects to the internet.

mainEntity.name: Do people get notified when you stop sharing an AirTag location?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you stop sharing an AirTag or someone stops sharing theirs with you, there is no notification. The AirTag no longer appears in the Items list or on the map, and their or your name is removed from the sharing section of the AirTag’s card.

mainEntity.name: Can multiple people track an AirTag?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Apple allows AirTag owners to share an AirTag’s location with up to 5 people using the Find My app.

mainEntity.name: Do deleted messages disappear everywhere?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once synced, deleted messages are removed from all devices.

mainEntity.name: Can messages sync without iCloud?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. iCloud is required for real-time iMessage syncing. Only SMS, MMS, and RCS messages can sync without iCloud using Text Message Forwarding.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a device is offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Messages will sync automatically once the device reconnects to the internet.

title.rendered: Siri Is Set to Become a Full AI Chatbot This Fall

content.rendered:
Apple is preparing one of the biggest changes to Siri since its launch. According to a new report from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman , the company plans to evolve Siri from a basic voice assistant into a full-fledged AI chatbot, starting later this year with upcoming software updates.

The change will roll out in stages, beginning with a major intelligence upgrade in iOS 26.4 and culminating in a completely redesigned Siri experience in iOS 27, macOS 27, and other Apple platforms.

A major intelligence upgrade arrives first

The first step comes with iOS 26.4, expected within the next two to three months. While Siri’s interface will look the same, its underlying technology will be completely replaced.

Apple will move Siri to Apple Foundation Models version 10, a system built on Google’s Gemini technology. This model reportedly uses 1.2 trillion parameters, making Siri significantly more capable than before.

With this update, Siri will gain the ability to search the web, understand what is happening on the screen, and take actions inside apps. It will also start using personal context, allowing responses to adapt based on how a user interacts with their device, rather than treating every request in isolation.

iOS 27 is where Siri becomes a chatbot

The bigger shift happens with iOS 27 and Apple’s 2027-era operating system updates. Internally, Apple refers to this version of Siri as “Campos.”

Instead of behaving like a simple listening assistant, Siri will move to a chat-style interface. Users will still activate it the same way, but interactions will feel more like a conversation. Siri will be able to answer detailed questions, search the web, generate text and images, and analyze uploaded files.

This marks Siri’s transition into the same category as modern AI chatbots, rather than a feature limited to quick commands.

Deeper control across apps and the system

One key advantage Siri will retain is deep integration with Apple’s ecosystem. The new chatbot version will understand open windows on macOS and on-screen content on iPhone and iPad.

This allows Siri to perform multi-step actions, suggest relevant commands, and work directly inside apps. It will continue to handle system-level controls such as device settings, smart home management, and everyday utilities.

Apple is also expanding Siri’s role inside its own apps, including Mail, Photos, Music, TV, Podcasts, and Xcode. This will let users issue more natural commands that involve searching, editing, or managing content without manually navigating through menus.

Privacy is still a limiting factor

Apple is reportedly being cautious about how much information Siri will be allowed to remember. While many AI chatbots store past interactions to improve responses, Apple is debating strict limits to protect user privacy.

This discussion is especially important as Apple considers whether some future cloud-based AI processing could rely on Google’s Gemini servers. For now, the Siri upgrade in iOS 26.4 will run on Apple’s own Private Cloud Compute infrastructure, powered by Apple Silicon.

Designed to evolve over time

The report also notes that Apple is building the new Siri in a modular way. This design allows Apple to swap out underlying AI models without reworking the entire assistant.

That flexibility gives Apple the option to move away from Gemini-based systems in the future, rely more heavily on its own models, or adapt Siri to meet regulatory requirements in specific regions.

If Apple delivers on these plans, Siri’s long-promised reinvention may finally arrive, turning it into a true AI assistant that can compete with modern chatbots while staying deeply tied to Apple’s devices and privacy approach.

excerpt.rendered: Apple is planning a major overhaul of Siri. Starting with iOS 26.4 and expanding fully in iOS 27, Siri is expected to evolve from a simple voice assistant into a full AI chatbot with web search, content creation, and deeper integration across Apple’s apps and devices.

mainEntity.name: Do people get notified when you stop sharing an AirTag location?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you stop sharing an AirTag or someone stops sharing theirs with you, there is no notification. The AirTag no longer appears in the Items list or on the map, and their or your name is removed from the sharing section of the AirTag’s card.

mainEntity.name: Can multiple people track an AirTag?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Apple allows AirTag owners to share an AirTag’s location with up to 5 people using the Find My app.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once synced, deleted messages are removed from all devices.

mainEntity.name: Can messages sync without iCloud?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. iCloud is required for real-time iMessage syncing. Only SMS, MMS, and RCS messages can sync without iCloud using Text Message Forwarding.

acceptedAnswer.text: Messages will sync automatically once the device reconnects to the internet.

title.rendered: Best MMORPG Games to Play in 2026

content.rendered:
Mobile MMORPGs have grown far beyond simple tap-and-play games. In 2026, they offer large open worlds, real-time combat, deep progression systems, and real multiplayer experiences that rival PC and console titles.

In this article, we’ve handpicked the best MMORPG games for iPhone and Android you should try in 2026. Whether you enjoy action-packed battles, proper sandboxing, or simply social adventures, this list is all about games that provide excellent performance, monetization, and long-term gameplay for mobile.

Table of Contents
  • What Makes a Great Mobile MMORPG in 2026?
  • Best MMORPG Games for iPhone and Android in 2026
    • 1. Genshin Impact
    • 2. Diablo Immortal
    • 3. Black Desert Mobile
    • 4. Wuthering Waves – To Lahai-Roi
    • 5. The Wolf: Animal Game MMORPG
    • 6. Albion Online
    • 7. Old School RuneScape
  • iPhone vs Android: Which Platform Is Better for MMORPGs?
    • Performance and Optimization
    • Ecosystem
    • Controllers Support and Cloud Gaming
  • Tips for Choosing the Right MMORPG for You
  • Final Verdict: Which MMORPG Should You Play in 2026?

What Makes a Great Mobile MMORPG in 2026?

A top-tier mobile MMORPG in 2026 isn’t just about flashy visuals. Here’s what truly matters:

  • Smooth performance on both mid-range and flagship devices.
  • Fair monetization to ensure skill and time matter more than in-app spending.
  • Flexible play styles, including short playthroughs and long grind sessions.
  • Community life with guilds, PvP action, and team play.
  • Cross-platform or cloud capability for convenience.

Best MMORPG Games for iPhone and Android in 2026

Here, I’ve listed the top 7 best MMORPG mobile games worth trying.

1. Genshin Impact

Genshin Impact continues to dominate the mobile MMORPG space. It delivers a massive open world, anime-style visuals, and fast-paced action combat that feels great on mobile. You can enjoy customizing your Manekins, surviving challenges in every stage, and creating your own world in Miliastra Sandbox.

Why you should play it:

  • Huge open world with constant updates
  • Cross-play with PC and console
  • Really good for solo players
  • Fair free-to-play experience (PvE-focused)

Best for: Players who enjoy exploration, story-driven content, and action combat without heavy PvP pressure.

Download: iPhone | Android

2. Diablo Immortal

This free-to-play action game comes with a classic Diablo dungeon experience with MMO features. You can explore shared online zones, team up in parties or guilds to get shared benefits, take on dungeon quests and world events, and battle hordes of demons in both solo and multiplayer modes.

Why you should play it:

  • Fast, satisfying combat
  • Constantly updating a dynamic world
  • Great co-op and PvE content
  • Strong community

Best for: Players who enjoy loot-based progression and fast-paced action.

Download: iPhone | Android

3. Black Desert Mobile

Black Desert Mobile is all about graphics, combat, and depth. Even in 2026, it remains one of the best-looking MMORPGs on mobile, with highly detailed characters and fast, flashy combat. The game provides you with vast life content, like fishing and your own camp to manage and expand, along with pets and horses.

Why you should play it:

  • Console-quality high-detail graphics
  • Deep character customization and world-building
  • Solid PvE or PvP game systems
  • Auto-play functions for casual gamers

Best for: Hardcore players who love to grind, engage in PvP, and complex systems of progression.

Download: iPhone | Android

4. Wuthering Waves – To Lahai-Roi

Are you looking for a fresh, story-rich game? Wuthering Waves is one of the most exciting newer MMO-style action RPGs. It focuses on smooth combat, darker themes, and stylish visuals, making it a strong alternative to Genshin Impact. The

Why you should play it:

  • Skill-based combat
  • Stylish, modern visuals
  • Easy controls optimized well for mobile
  • Growing global community

Best for: A player seeking challenging battles and a modern anime setting.

Download: iPhone | Android

5. The Wolf: Animal Game MMORPG

If you’re tired of playing fantasy RPGS, here’s a unique one where you play as a wolf surviving in a multiplayer ecosystem. It’s simple, creative, and surprisingly social. You get various gameplay modes, character customization options, and smooth performance with beautiful environments.

Why you should play it:

  • Unique animal-based gameplay
  • Easy to learn, hard to master
  • Strong co-op and PvP mechanics
  • Realistic graphics

Best for: Casual players or those looking for something different from fantasy MMOs.

Download: iPhone | Android

6. Albion Online

Albion Online is one of the most player-driven MMORPGs available on mobile. Everything, from gear, playstyle to the economy, is controlled by players. You can play sandbox MMO RPG with millions of users, also create your own guild, or engage in massive battles with 20 versus 20.

Why you should play it:

  • True cross-platform gameplay
  • Full loot PvP for risk-takers
  • Deep crafting and trading systems
  • No pay-to-win mechanics

Best for: Gamers who enjoy strategic gameplay, economy management, and all-out PvP battles with sandbox freedom.

Download: iPhone | Android

7. Old School RuneScape

Old School RuneScape proves that great classic gameplay never gets old. It offers the full PC experience on mobile with very few compromises. Its epic puzzles and quests will amuse you a lot if you like lore-rich narratives sprinkled with nostalgic humor.

Why you should play it:

  • Massive world with endless content
  • Strong community-driven updates
  • Works perfectly for short and long sessions
  • Very fair monetization

Best for: Players who love classic MMO design and long-term progression.

Download: iPhone | Android

iPhone vs Android: Which Platform Is Better for MMORPGs?

When it comes to playing MMORPGs on mobile, both iPhone and Android offer excellent experiences. The better choice really depends on your device, preferences, and how you like to play.

Performance and Optimization

  • iPhone games are normally better optimized in terms of smooth frame rates and fewer bugs.
  • Android performance varies by device. High-end Android phones run MMORPGs just as well as iPhones, but lower-end models may struggle with graphics-heavy games.

Ecosystem

  • iOS provides a more consistent experience with longer software update support and gaming mode, which is great for long-term MMO players.
  • Android supports emulators and mod-friendly setups.

Controllers Support and Cloud Gaming

  • Both platforms now support Bluetooth controllers, making action MMORPGs more comfortable to play.
  • Cloud gaming platforms are quite functional on both iOS and Android, enabling you to play complex MMORPGs without having to rely on your phone’s processing capabilities entirely.

If you value smooth performance and long-term updates, iPhone is a strong choice. If you prefer customization and flexibility, Android is just as good. Your focus should be on having a capable device and a stable internet connection.

Tips for Choosing the Right MMORPG for You

With so many mobile MMORPGs available in 2026, choosing the right one can feel overwhelming. The best game for you depends on how you like to play, how much time you have, and what kind of experience you want.

Here are a few simple tips to help you decide:

  • Casual or hardcore: If you only play in short sessions, look for MMORPGs with auto-play, daily quests, and flexible progression. However, hardcore gamers can go for games featuring intricate combat systems and long-term goals.
  • Solo or guild-focused games: Some MMORPGs are great for solo players with good storytelling and tasks you can manage alone. Other MMORPGs might center around guilds, group PvP combat, or other teamwork aspects.
  • PvE or PvP? If you enjoy fighting monsters, exploring worlds, and following a story, choose a game with strong PvE content. If competition excites you, look for MMORPGs with balanced PvP, arenas, or open-world battles.
  • Time Investment: An MMORPG may require daily login sessions with extensive grinding, while others understand the worth of your time, allowing you to progress at your own pace.
  • Monetization and Fairness: Always check how the game handles in-app purchases. The best MMORPGs let you enjoy most of the content for free and avoid heavy pay-to-win systems.

Final Verdict: Which MMORPG Should You Play in 2026?

Those mobile MMORPGs in 2026 will be even more player-friendly, powerful, and flexible. No matter your playstyle or budget, there’s a game on this list worth trying.

title.rendered: Apple’s Next Month at a Glance: Key Dates to Watch From Late January to February 2026

content.rendered:
Apple’s early 2026 calendar is finally taking shape, and the weeks ahead signal a clear shift from a quiet start to a much busier stretch. While there is still no confirmed product launch on the horizon, Apple has lined up several important dates that touch its services, retail presence, developer ecosystem, and financial performance. Together, they offer a clear snapshot of where the company’s focus lies as the year gains momentum.

January 23: Apple Relocates Its Santa Rosa Retail Store

Apple’s first confirmed date arrives on January 23, when its Santa Rosa retail store in California reopens at a new location in Montgomery Village.

Retail store moves are often overlooked, but Apple treats them as an extension of its brand. New locations typically reflect updated store layouts, greater emphasis on services, and redesigned spaces for product demos and support.

January 28: Apple Creator Studio Officially Launches

One of the most notable developments comes on January 28 with the launch of Apple Creator Studio.

The new subscription bundle brings together Apple’s professional creative apps under a single plan. It includes tools for video editing, music production, motion graphics, and image editing, along with premium content across several Apple apps.

This launch highlights Apple’s growing focus on creators, positioning its software ecosystem as a long-term alternative to standalone app purchases and third-party creative suites.

January 29: Apple Reports Holiday Quarter Earnings

A day later, on January 29, Apple will report its earnings for the first quarter of its 2026 fiscal year, which covers the critical holiday shopping season.

The earnings call is expected to shed light on how Apple’s latest hardware updates performed during the holidays. Apple’s leadership will discuss the results during a live conference call, offering insight into sales trends and overall business performance, even if future plans remain closely guarded.

February 5: New Games Arrive on Apple Arcade

Apple Arcade continues to expand its library, with four new games arriving on February 5.

The upcoming additions include a retro-style arcade experience featuring classic titles, as well as an arcade adaptation of a popular strategy game. The update reinforces Apple’s steady investment in subscription-based, ad-free gaming across its platforms.

February 6: Swift Student Challenge Opens for 2026

On February 6, Apple will begin accepting submissions for the 2026 Swift Student Challenge.

The annual program gives students an opportunity to showcase their coding skills using Swift. Select winners will earn an invitation to visit Apple Park during WWDC 2026, making it one of Apple’s most visible efforts to engage the next generation of developers.

February 8: Apple Music Takes Center Stage at the Super Bowl

Apple Music takes on a high-profile role on February 8 as the official sponsor of the Super Bowl halftime show.

The partnership underscores Apple’s push to turn Apple Music into a cultural brand, using major live events to extend its reach beyond traditional music streaming.

February 10: Apple Ends Support for Older Home App Architecture

February 10 marks an important transition for Apple Home users. On this day, Apple will end support for the original Home app architecture.

Users who have not updated to the newer system may experience reliability issues, signaling Apple’s continued move toward a more modern and unified smart home platform.

Also read: Apple’s homeOS: Everything you need to know

February 24: Apple Holds Its Annual Shareholders Meeting

The month wraps up on February 24, when Apple holds its annual shareholders meeting. The event will once again take place virtually.

While these meetings are typically procedural, they remain a formal checkpoint for Apple’s leadership and investors, even if major announcements are unlikely.

The Bigger Picture

Taken together, these dates show Apple laying important groundwork rather than chasing headlines with new products. Services, subscriptions, and developer engagement are clearly in focus, while behind-the-scenes changes continue across retail and smart home platforms.

Hardware announcements may still come unexpectedly, but even without them, Apple’s next few weeks reveal a company steadily setting the tone for the rest of 2026.

title.rendered: Apple Pay May Finally Launch in India by the End of 2026

content.rendered:
After years of waiting, Apple Pay may finally be on track to arrive in India. According to a Business Standard report, Apple is working behind the scenes with banks, regulators, and card networks to launch the service in the country by the end of 2026.

Apple is Reportedly Working With Banks and Regulators

The report claims Apple is already coordinating with Indian banks, regulators, and major card networks to make Apple Pay available in the country. As with any Apple Pay expansion, approvals and back-end partnerships will decide the timeline.

Tap to Pay on iPhone May Also Arrive Alongside Apple Pay

Once Apple Pay launches, Apple is also expected to introduce Tap to Pay on iPhone in India. This feature allows an iPhone to accept contactless payments directly via NFC, enabling businesses to take payments without a separate card machine in supported scenarios.

However, the report mentions that Apple will still need to negotiate fees with major card issuers to enable Apple Pay’s payment gateway.

UPI is the Real Challenge, and Apple May Avoid It for Now

While India’s digital payments ecosystem is dominated by UPI, Apple may not pursue the third-party app provider approvals needed to integrate with UPI in the near term. Instead, the initial Apple Pay rollout could be more card-based, as it does in other global markets.

Apple Pay has already been used indirectly in India for international payments. Last year, Cashfree Payments and Razorpay integrated Apple Pay to support international payments for Indian merchants.

Apple Pay is Already Live in 89 Markets

Apple Pay launched more than a decade ago and is currently available in 89 markets worldwide, making India one of the most prominent missing regions.

Why This Timing Makes Sense for Apple

The potential launch aligns with Apple’s momentum in India. The company reportedly recorded its highest quarterly shipments in the country in Q3 2025, hitting 5 million units and reaching fourth place in market rankings for the first time, per IDC figures.

Do you want Apple Pay in India, or does UPI already cover everything you need? Let us know in the comments.

title.rendered: How to Turn Off Autocorrect on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

content.rendered:
Autocorrect is one such iPhone feature that looks very useful on paper, but in reality, it quickly turns into a headache. It is why your “Yes bro” becomes “Yes brp”, your friend’s name changes to something random, and your perfectly fine Hinglish sentence turns into a grammatical crime scene.

And the worst part is that it sometimes even replaces correct words and brand names. So if you are tired of fighting your keyboard every day, it’s time to switch autocorrect off. This post details how to disable autocorrect on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

Table of Contents
  • What Autocorrect Actually Does on iPhone, iPad, and Mac
  • Difference Between Auto-Correction and Predictive Text
  • How to Turn Off Auto-Correction on iPhone
    • Via Settings
    • Directly via Keyboard
  • How to Turn Off Auto-Correction on Mac
  • How to Turn Off Auto-Correction for Certain Words on iPhone
  • Does Turning Off Auto-Correction Affect All Apps?
  • Autocorrect is Off, But iPhone Still Changes Words? Try These Fixes
    • Summing Up…

What Autocorrect Actually Does on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

First things first, autocorrect on iPhone and iPad is referred to as Auto-Correction. It comes enabled by default on iPhone and iPad and tries to:

  • Fix spelling mistakes automatically.
  • Replace “incorrect” words with what it thinks you meant.
  • Sometimes, change words after you finish typing or even after you hit send.

In short, autocorrect is not just a typing helper. It can literally rewrite parts of your message without warning.

On Mac, Apple labels autocorrect a little differently. Instead of Auto-Correction, you’ll usually see the toggle labeled “Correct spelling automatically. This is the macOS version of autocorrect, and it works across most Apple apps (and many third-party apps, too).

Difference Between Auto-Correction and Predictive Text

This is where many people get confused because both features are related to typing, but they behave very differently.

How to Turn Off Auto-Correction on iPhone

Turning off Auto-Correction on iPhone is pretty straightforward and can be done in two ways:

Via Settings

This is the most reliable method and works across all apps.

  1. Open Settings and tap General.
  2. Here, locate and tap Keyboard.
  3. Next, toggle off Auto-Correction under All Keyboards.

Once done, your iPhone will stop replacing your words automatically.

Directly via Keyboard

While turning off Auto-Correction in Settings is pretty quick, it’s inconvenient when you are already typing in an app and have to close it because of it. In that case, you can quickly jump to keyboard settings directly from the keyboard. Here is how:

  1. Open any app that uses the keyboard.
  2. Tap and hold the Globe (Emoji) icon at the bottom-left corner of the keyboard.
  3. Tap Keyboard Settings on the pop-up menu that appears.
  4. Toggle off Auto-Correction under All keyboards.

Note: If you don’t see a globe key, it’s usually because you only have one keyboard language enabled. In that case, you may see an emoji icon instead.

How to Turn Off Auto-Correction on Mac

Mac keyboard settings do not automatically mirror your iPhone keyboard settings, even if both devices are signed in with the same Apple ID. So turning off autocorrect on iPhone won’t turn it off on your Mac, and vice versa.

  1. Open the Settings app and select Keyboard in the sidebar.
  2. Here, click the Edit button next to Input Sources under Text Input.
  3. Toggle off “Correct spelling automatically.”

How to Turn Off Auto-Correction for Certain Words on iPhone

If you don’t want to turn off Auto-Correction entirely, you do have a smarter option. You can stop your iPhone from “fixing” specific words (like your name, your city, brand names, slang, or Hinglish phrases) by adding them to the keyboard dictionary using Text Replacement.

  1. Open Settings → General → Keyboard.
  2. Tap Text Replace ment.
  3. Tap the + button at the top right corner.
  4. In the Phrase field, type the word you want iPhone to accept (example: Vikhyat, iGeeksBlog, Hinglish)
  5. In the Shortcut field, type the same word again
  6. Tap Save.

Once done, your iPhone will not auto-correct the exact word, even with Auto-Correction enabled.

Does Turning Off Auto-Correction Affect All Apps?

Yes, the Auto-Correction toggle on iPhone and Mac applies system-wide. When you switch off Auto Correction, autocorrect will stop working in:

  • iMessage and WhatsApp.
  • Instagram captions and DMs.
  • Notes.
  • Safari search.
  • Gmail and other mail apps.
  • Any third-party app that uses the keyboard.

Apple currently does not offer a per-app or per-keyboard autocorrect toggle.

Autocorrect is Off, But iPhone Still Changes Words? Try These Fixes

Even after you disable Auto Correction, iOS can still interfere with typing through other “smart” features. These settings are worth checking.

Summing Up…

And that’s it; this is how you turn off autocorrect on your Apple devices and make typing feel faster, cleaner, and more in your control. Remember, you do not need to turn off autocorrect completely if the issues are with specific words, such as names, slang, or brand terms. In such cases, Text Replacement is a better solution.

Did turning off autocorrect fix the issue for you? Share your experience in the comments and tell us which iPhone or Mac keyboard setting annoys you the most

FAQs

Can I turn off autocorrect for one app only?

No. iOS doesn’t currently offer per-app autocorrect controls.

Can I turn autocorrect off for only one language?

The Auto-Correction setting applies to all keyboards, though behavior can vary depending on the language.

excerpt.rendered: Autocorrect can be helpful, but it’s not for everyone. Learn how to turn off autocorrect on your iPhone, iPad, and Mac in just a few easy steps.

mainEntity.name: Do people get notified when you stop sharing an AirTag location?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you stop sharing an AirTag or someone stops sharing theirs with you, there is no notification. The AirTag no longer appears in the Items list or on the map, and their or your name is removed from the sharing section of the AirTag’s card.

mainEntity.name: Can multiple people track an AirTag?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Apple allows AirTag owners to share an AirTag’s location with up to 5 people using the Find My app.

mainEntity.name: Do deleted messages disappear everywhere?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once synced, deleted messages are removed from all devices.

mainEntity.name: Can messages sync without iCloud?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. iCloud is required for real-time iMessage syncing. Only SMS, MMS, and RCS messages can sync without iCloud using Text Message Forwarding.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a device is offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Messages will sync automatically once the device reconnects to the internet.

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

title.rendered: How to Use Apple Handoff Feature: A Complete Guide

content.rendered:
Switching between devices while working may feel like starting over. That’s exactly the problem Apple Handoff solves. When you use your iPhone, iPad, and Mac simultaneously, this feature lets you continue working from where you left off on another device without saving or syncing anything.

In this guide, you’ll learn how Apple Handoff works and how to use it to make your Apple devices feel like one seamless workspace.

Table of Contents
  • What is Apple Handoff?
  • How Apple Handoff Works
    • Continuity Features Ecosystem
  • Requirements for Apple Handoff
  • How to Turn On Handoff for Your Apple Device
    • On iPhone and iPad
    • On Mac
    • On Apple Watch
  • How to Use the Handoff Feature Between iPhone and iPad
    • Tips for Switching Back and Forth
  • How to Use the Handoff Feature Between iPhone/iPad and Mac
    • Example Workflows
  • Supported Handoff Apps
  • Troubleshooting Apple Handoff
  • Advanced Tips for Power Users
    • Handoff in Multitasking Workflows
    • Using Handoff With Sidecar and Universal Control
    • Best Practices to Speed Up Device Discovery
  • Final Thoughts

What is Apple Handoff?

Apple Handoff is a Continuity feature from Apple that allows you to move an active task, like writing an email, browsing a website, or editing a note, from one Apple device to another instantly. You can begin on your iPhone and finish on your Mac, or start on your Mac and continue on your iPad, right where you left off.

What makes Handoff special is that it works automatically in the background. There’s no “export,” no file sharing, and no extra steps. As long as your devices are nearby and signed in to the same Apple ID, Handoff just appears when you need it.

It feels less like syncing and more like your devices are one extended workspace.

How Apple Handoff Works

Handoff relies on two key technologies:

  • Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) to detect nearby devices
  • Wi-Fi to transfer activity data quickly and securely

Bluetooth handles discovery (finding devices in range), whereas Wi-Fi handles the actual data transfer. And note that only activity metadata is shared, not full app data. For example:

  • A Safari webpage link
  • A draft email state
  • Ongoing FaceTime call

All communication is encrypted, and Apple cannot read your activities. Also, Handoff itself does not upload your work to the cloud in real time.

Continuity Features Ecosystem

Handoff is part of Apple’s larger Continuity ecosystem, which includes:

  • Handoff: Continue apps across devices.
  • Universal Clipboard: Copy on one device, paste on another.
  • AirDrop: Fast file sharing.
  • Universal Control: Use one keyboard and mouse across devices.
  • Sidecar: Use iPad as a Mac display.
  • Continuity Camera: Use iPhone as a webcam for Mac and Apple TV.

There are more such features like AirPlay, Auto Unlock, iPhone Mirroring, etc., and together they make Apple devices feel deeply connected rather than separate.

Requirements for Apple Handoff

Handoff works across almost all Apple devices, including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Apple Vision Pro. Keep the devices updated to the latest OS version for smooth operations.

To work properly, all devices must:

  • Be signed in to iCloud using the same Apple ID
  • Have Wi-Fi and Bluetooth turned on
  • Have Handoff enabled in settings
  • Placed within close proximity (30 feet)

How to Turn On Handoff for Your Apple Device

Now that you understand the feature well, let’s set it up.

On iPhone and iPad

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap General
  3. Select AirPlay & Continuity.
  4. Toggle on Handoff.

On Mac

  1. Click the Apple Menu at the top and open System Settings.
  2. Go to General from the left sidebar.
  3. Click AirDrop & Handoff.
  4. Scroll down and toggle on Allow Handoff between this Mac and your iCloud devices.

On Apple Watch

Apple has also integrated this swift feature into the Apple Watch so that you can start a task on your watch and complete it on your iPhone or Mac.

  1. Launch the Watch app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap General from the My Watch tab.
  3. Toggle on Enable Handoff.

How to Use the Handoff Feature Between iPhone and iPad

Here comes the fun part! Follow these steps to quickly hand off your tasks:

  1. Open a supported app, like Mail or Safari, and begin working normally.
  2. On the iPad Dock, you’ll see an app icon at the right end.
  3. To continue on your iPhone, swipe up from the bottom of your screen and hold to open App Switcher.
  4. You will see a banner showing the Handoff app from your nearby Apple device.
  5. Tap it, and the app opens exactly where you left off.

If you have an Apple Watch, you can hand off a lot of apps to your iPhone, such as Activity, Alarm, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Phone, Podcasts, Reminders, Settings, Stopwatch, Timers, Wallet, Weather, etc.

Tips for Switching Back and Forth

  • Keep both devices unlocked for faster detection.
  • Use strong Wi-Fi for near-instant transitions.
  • Don’t force-close apps you want to hand off.

How to Use the Handoff Feature Between iPhone/iPad and Mac

  1. When you start an activity on iOS or iPadOS, a Handoff icon appears on your Mac.
  2. On the Mac Dock near the left side, you will see the app icon itself with a small phone logo.
  3. Click once to open the app with your active session. You can also press Command + Tab keys to quickly switch to the Handoff app.

Example Workflows

I frequently use Handoff for day-to-day tasks because it saves time and keeps my productivity high.

  • Browse an article on iPhone → finish reading on Mac.
  • Start an email on iPad → send it from Mac to attach files.
  • Edit a note on iPhone → continue on iPad for Apple Pencil features.
  • Start a FaceTime call on iPhone → continue on Mac. The FaceTime Handoff also works across Apple TV.
  • Start shopping with Apple Pay on Mac → Complete the purchase on iPhone or Apple Watch.

The most useful feature is Universal Clipboard, which lets you copy text, images, and videos from one device and simply paste them on another.

Supported Handoff Apps

Handoff works best with Apple’s own apps:

  • Safari
  • Mail
  • Contacts
  • Maps
  • Notes
  • FaceTime
  • Calendar
  • Reminders
  • Pages
  • Numbers
  • Keynote

Many third-party apps, such as Quip and The Wall Street Journal, also support Handoff. When supported, the experience looks identical to Apple apps, no setup needed.

Troubleshooting Apple Handoff

Like other Continuity features, Handoff works smoothly. However, it can sometimes experience hiccups. Here are some common issues and quick solutions you can try.

If you are still facing issues, you may contact Apple Support.

Advanced Tips for Power Users

Want to boost your productivity? These tips will help you out:

Handoff in Multitasking Workflows

On iPad, combine Handoff with:

  • Split View
  • Stage Manager

This lets you continue a task while running multiple apps side by side. You can also use your iPad to sketch and markup on your Mac documents and see the changes in real-time on the Mac screen.

Using Handoff With Sidecar and Universal Control

Handoff works beautifully alongside Sidecar and Universal Control, letting you:

  • Use iPad as a second display for your Mac.
  • Control everything with one keyboard and mouse, creating an extended workplace.

Best Practices to Speed Up Device Discovery

  • Keep Wi-Fi on even when using Ethernet.
  • Avoid low-power Bluetooth accessories interfering.
  • Don’t disable background app refresh.

Final Thoughts

Apple Handoff is one of those features that quietly changes how you work. Once enabled, it removes friction, saves time, and makes your iPhone, iPad, and Mac feel like one continuous device rather than three separate devices.

If you live inside the Apple ecosystem, learning to use Handoff well is one of the easiest productivity upgrades you can make in 2026.

Which is your favorite Continuity feature? Let us know in the comments below!

FAQs

Does Handoff Work on Public Wi-Fi?

Yes. As long as Bluetooth is enabled and devices are signed into the same Apple ID, public Wi-Fi works fine.

Can You Disable Handoff for Specific Apps?

No. Handoff is system-wide. You can only enable or disable it globally.

Why Doesn’t Handoff Work With Locked Screens?

Handoff requires authentication. Fully locked devices may delay or block session transfer for security reasons.

mainEntity.name: Do people get notified when you stop sharing an AirTag location?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you stop sharing an AirTag or someone stops sharing theirs with you, there is no notification. The AirTag no longer appears in the Items list or on the map, and their or your name is removed from the sharing section of the AirTag’s card.

mainEntity.name: Can multiple people track an AirTag?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Apple allows AirTag owners to share an AirTag’s location with up to 5 people using the Find My app.

mainEntity.name: Do deleted messages disappear everywhere?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once synced, deleted messages are removed from all devices.

mainEntity.name: Can messages sync without iCloud?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. iCloud is required for real-time iMessage syncing. Only SMS, MMS, and RCS messages can sync without iCloud using Text Message Forwarding.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a device is offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Messages will sync automatically once the device reconnects to the internet.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. iOS doesn’t currently offer per-app autocorrect controls.

mainEntity.name: Does Handoff Work on Public Wi-Fi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. As long as Bluetooth is enabled and devices are signed into the same Apple ID, public Wi-Fi works fine.

mainEntity.name: Can You Disable Handoff for Specific Apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Handoff is system-wide. You can only enable or disable it globally.

title.rendered: Apple Reclaims Top Spot in China Smartphone Market in Q4 2025

content.rendered:
Apple returned to the top of China’s smartphone market in the fourth quarter of 2025, marking a sharp turnaround after a challenging year. The company’s resurgence came at a time when the overall market was contracting, highlighting the impact of strong demand for its latest iPhone lineup during the holiday season.

A Market Under Pressure

According to Counterpoint Research, China’s smartphone shipments declined year over year in the fourth quarter, reflecting weaker consumer demand. Rising component and memory prices pushed device costs higher, making buyers more cautious and putting pressure on most major brands operating in the country.

Against this backdrop, Apple stood out. The company recorded strong shipment growth in China during the quarter, allowing it to capture a 22 percent market share and secure first place, even as the broader market moved in the opposite direction.

iPhone 17 Powered Apple’s Comeback

The iPhone 17 lineup was the primary driver behind Apple’s Q4 performance. A significant share of the company’s China shipments came from these models, with the Pro variants attracting the strongest interest. The lineup helped Apple appeal to buyers who were still willing to spend on premium devices despite rising prices.

Apple’s improved supply situation also played a role. With a faster ramp-up toward the end of the year, the company was better positioned to meet holiday demand, while some competitors continued to face component-related constraints.

iPhone Air Lagged Behind

Not all models contributed equally to Apple’s rebound. The iPhone Air saw limited traction in China during the quarter. Its later launch and trade-offs linked to its ultra-thin design held back demand, leaving it with only a small share of Apple’s total shipments compared to other iPhone 17 models.

Full-Year Rankings Tell a Different Story

Despite Apple’s strong finish, the full-year picture remained highly competitive. Huawei emerged as the leading smartphone brand in China for 2025, with Apple and vivo close behind. Xiaomi and Oppo followed, underscoring how narrow the gap was between the top players throughout the year.

Globally, Apple maintained its leadership position. Worldwide smartphone shipments saw modest growth in 2025, and Apple remained the largest smartphone vendor by shipment volume.

Rising Costs Could Shape 2026

Looking ahead, the outlook for the smartphone market remains uncertain. Memory prices are expected to rise further in early 2026, which could increase device prices and pressure margins. Manufacturers may respond by reducing their focus on low-end models and relying more heavily on subsidies to sustain demand.

Apple’s Q4 performance in China shows that strong flagship appeal and solid supply execution can still deliver results in a difficult market. Whether that momentum carries into 2026 will depend largely on pricing trends and how competition evolves in the months ahead.

title.rendered: 10 Best Stranger Things Wallpapers for iPhone (Download in 4K)

content.rendered:
The final season of Stranger Things has officially dropped, and fans everywhere are soaking in the nostalgia, chaos, and emotional goodbyes. If you’re not ready to leave Hawkins just yet, the easiest way to keep the vibe alive is with a Stranger Things wallpaper.

In this guide, I’ve curated the best Stranger Things wallpapers for iPhone in 4K, inspired by the show’s most iconic visuals from bikes at sunset to the terrifying Upside Down. So, you can easily pick one that matches your mood.

Table of Contents
  • 1. Stranger Things Red Sky Background
  • 2. Minimal Pink Upside Down Silhouette
  • 3. Storm Over Hawkins Road
  • 4. Upside Down Stranger Things Wallpaper
  • 5. Scary Demogorgon Close-Up
  • 6. Stranger Things Poster Wallpaper
  • 7. Upside Down Reflection Bike Scene
  • 8. Stranger Things Fan Art
  • 9. Stranger Things Logo Wallpaper
  • 10. Will Buyers Stranger Things Wallpaper
  • Final Thoughts

1. Stranger Things Red Sky Background

This wallpaper is pure Stranger Things nostalgia. It shows the group riding their bikes as the sun sets in Hawkins, with dramatic red clouds filling the sky.

Download

2. Minimal Pink Upside Down Silhouette

Next is a clean, minimalist design with bike silhouettes on top and the Upside Down reflected below in soft pink tones.

Download

3. Storm Over Hawkins Road

All Stranger Things fans know this iconic scene. The supreme ruler of Upside Down, Mind-Flayer, appears in Hawkins. The wallpaper is equally scary and intriguin

Download

4. Upside Down Stranger Things Wallpaper

A dramatic Stranger Things wallpaper featuring Will Byers staring out into the fiery red sky of the Upside Down. The dark aesthetic with an apocalyptic glow is truly iconic.

Download

5. Scary Demogorgon Close-Up

If you love scary wallpaper, download this one. It shows a terrifying Demogorgon emerging from a dark forest, giving a horror effect to your screen.

Download

6. Stranger Things Poster Wallpaper

A colorful and neon-lit collage artwork featuring Eleven and the entire cast. It’s best for the fans who want to celebrate the entire Stranger Things journey.

Download

7. Upside Down Reflection Bike Scene

Following is an artistic wallpaper showing members on bikes, with their dark reflections below them. This design visually explains the show’s core idea at one glance.

Download

8. Stranger Things Fan Art

Explosions, red lightning, floating objects, and a lone rider in the center; this fan-edited wallpaper screams Stranger Things chaos.

Download

9. Stranger Things Logo Wallpaper

A split design featuring the show’s logo above the light and the Upside Down below. Great for minimalists who still want to show their Stranger Things love.

Download

10. Will Buyers Stranger Things Wallpaper

A dark and intense wallpaper featuring Will Byers channeling supernatural power. Not a spoiler, but this scene has turned the tables in the season finale climax.

Download

Final Thoughts

Now that the final season of Stranger Things is here, these wallpapers feel more meaningful than ever. They’re not just backgrounds; they’re reminders of friendships, fear, bravery, and one unforgettable ride through Hawkins.

Pick the one that hits you right in the feels, set it on your phone, and keep the Stranger Things universe alive.

Which Stranger Things character do you like the most? Let me know in the comments below!

  • Mind-Warping Doctor Strange Wallpapers
  • Batman Wallpapers for iPhone
  • Web-Tastic Spiderman iPhone Wallpapers

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro Might Move Dynamic Island from Center, Leak Hints

content.rendered:
Apple’s next iPhone 18 Pro models might deliver a noticeable change to the front display design. According to recent leaks, the Dynamic Island could shift from its current central location.

A new video from leaker Jon Prosser on Front Page Tech suggests that Apple may introduce under-display Face ID technology in the iPhone 18 Pro lineup. This change could prompt a move for the selfie camera to the top-left corner, appearing as a smaller punch-hole cutout.

Dynamic Island’s New Placement May Follow Camera Shift

Prosser speculates that if the selfie camera ends up in the top-left corner, Apple might also relocate the Dynamic Island interface to that same spot. Instead of unfolding from the middle, it would animate outward from the top-left, continuing to deliver Live Activities, alerts, timers, and background app indicators.

Since its introduction on the iPhone 14 Pro models, the Dynamic Island has remained dead-center. It’s an interactive element where Apple transformed the sensor cutout into something more functional than a static notch.

More Leads on Under-Display Face ID

While Prosser’s claim is fresh, the notion of under-display Face ID for the iPhone 18 Pro has circulated from other sources as well.

The Information had previously reported that Apple may conceal much of the Face ID sensors under the display, leaving only a modest punch-hole camera cutout positioned in the top-left corner.

However, iGeeksBlog points out that Prosser’s insights regarding the Dynamic Island might stem from assumptions rather than independent verification, as Apple might choose other UI redesign paths.

Apple Could Opt to Keep Dynamic Island in the Middle

Former display analyst Ross Young suggests that even with under-display Face ID, Apple might preserve the Dynamic Island’s central position by compressing it into a tinier pill or hole design. This would allow Apple to retain the current interface function without moving a significant element to one side.

Thus, though speculation about a top-left camera arrangement is conceivable, it’s not definite that the Dynamic Island will follow suit.

Additional iPhone 18 Pro Features Under Discussion

Prosser’s report also revisits other circulating iPhone 18 Pro rumors, which include:

  • New colorways like burgundy, brown, and purple
  • A variable aperture camera system
  • A simplified Camera Control button
  • The A20 Pro chip
  • Apple’s C2 modem
  • Expanded satellite features

Apple is anticipated to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro lineup in September 2026.

Would the idea of the Dynamic Island moving to the top-left corner on the iPhone 18 Pro make any difference to you? Share your perspective in the comments section.

excerpt.rendered: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro could bring a major display tweak, with leaks hinting that the Dynamic Island may move from the center if under-display Face ID is introduced. The change could shift the selfie camera and interface toward the top-left corner.

mainEntity.name: Do people get notified when you stop sharing an AirTag location?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you stop sharing an AirTag or someone stops sharing theirs with you, there is no notification. The AirTag no longer appears in the Items list or on the map, and their or your name is removed from the sharing section of the AirTag’s card.

mainEntity.name: Can multiple people track an AirTag?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Apple allows AirTag owners to share an AirTag’s location with up to 5 people using the Find My app.

title.rendered: Best Keyboard Apps for iPhone and Android in 2026

content.rendered:
Let’s be honest. Your phone keyboard is the one app you use all day without realizing it, yet it is rarely treated like the power tool it is. Every DM, email, caption, and search begins there. Still, while we swap launchers, change wallpapers, and obsess over camera apps, we often stick with the pre-installed keyboard, even when it slows us down.

Having a better keyboard app installed can improve speed, autocorrect, predictions, and multilingual typing, making everyday typing smoother and more accurate. That’s why choosing the right keyboard app matters more than most people realize.

With that in mind, here are the five best keyboard apps for iPhone and Android that genuinely improve your typing experience.

Table of Contents
  • How I Evaluated the Best Keyboard Apps
  • 5 Best Keyboard Apps for iOS and Android
  • 1. Gboard (Google Keyboard)
    • 2. Microsoft SwiftKey
    • 3. Grammarly Keyboard
    • 4. Typewise
    • 5. Bitmoji Keyboard
  • Key Features to Look for in a Keyboard App
  • Choose the Right Keyboard App…

How I Evaluated the Best Keyboard Apps

There are thousands of third-party keyboard apps available on the App Store and Play Store. So, it is easy to feel overwhelmed. To help you choose the best options, I evaluated each keyboard the way most people actually use it.

  • Typing accuracy and predictions: How often autocorrect messed up, and how naturally suggestions matched my typing style.
  • Swipe and voice typing: Swipe speed and accuracy, plus how well voice typing worked in noisy places.
  • Multilingual support: How smoothly the keyboard handled switching between languages without breaking the flow.
  • Customization: Themes, layouts, font options, and how much you can tweak the look and feel.
  • Productivity tools: Clipboard history, shortcuts, and cursor control that actually help save time.
  • Privacy and permissions: What permissions it asks for and how transparent it is about data use.
  • Performance: Any lag, stutters, or battery drain over longer periods of use.
  • iPhone vs Android differences: How much the experience changes due to iOS restrictions vs Android freedom.

5 Best Keyboard Apps for iOS and Android

After trying out several popular options, these are the best keyboard apps for iPhone and Android that actually improve day-to-day typing.

1. Gboard (Google Keyboard)

If you want a keyboard with no learning curve, I recommend Gboard. In my experience, it’s the most balanced keyboard across both iPhone and Android.

What I like most is how accurate it feels without being aggressive. Predictions are on point, swipe typing is smooth, and voice typing is easily one of the best parts of the app. If I had to pick one keyboard for any phone, it would be this.

Pros

  • Reliable autocorrect and predictions
  • Excellent voice typing
  • Smooth swipe typing

Download: iPhone | Android

Cons

  • Not the most customizable option

2. Microsoft SwiftKey

SwiftKey is the keyboard I use when I want typing to feel effortless. It has the best mind-reading style predictions after Gboard, and in some cases, I would say it even beats Gboard for casual chatting.

This keyboard app adapts to your tone and vocabulary over time, helping you type fewer words manually as you go. Another thing I genuinely like is the clipboard feature. When I’m repeatedly pasting one-time passcodes, addresses, or links, SwiftKey speeds up that workflow. It is the keyboard I pick when I’m in peak messaging mode.

Pros

  • Excellent predictions that improve with time
  • Clipboard tools are genuinely useful
  • Great for bilingual users

Download: iPhone | Android

Cons

  • The interface can feel slightly busy

3. Grammarly Keyboard

First things first, the Grammarly Keyboard is not for everyone. It is extremely useful when writing something public facing, such as an email, Instagram caption, or professional message.

Unlike regular keyboards that only fix spelling, Grammarly catches grammar slips, punctuation issues, and awkward phrasing as you type. You can think of it as the closest thing to having an editor running in the background.

Pros

  • Improves writing quality instantly
  • Great for emails and long-form typing
  • Helps with tone and clarity

Download: iPhone | Android

Cons

  • Not necessary for casual chat users
  • Some suggestions require a premium

4. Typewise

If you want a cleaner, more privacy-first option, the Typewise keyboard is one you must check out. In my testing, it feels less “data-hungry” than many feature-packed keyboards, and it focuses more on typing accuracy than flashy extras.

What’s interesting is its Hexagon layout, designed to reduce typos. While it does take a little adjustment, it’s surprisingly effective once you get used to it. Even if you don’t use the hexagon layout, Typewise still feels like a solid keyboard that’s built for people who want control.

Pros

  • Privacy-first approach
  • Reduced typing mistakes over time
  • Clean and minimal interface

Download: iPhone | Android

Cons

  • The hexagon layout takes time to adapt to

5. Bitmoji Keyboard

Unlike other keyboard apps on this list, the Bitmoji Keyboard is not a productivity keyboard. It is a fun add-on I use when I want conversations to feel more expressive. Instead of jumping between apps to find stickers, I can drop Bitmojis right from the keyboard, which works especially well on WhatsApp, Instagram DMs, iMessage, and Snapchat.

If you like reacting with stickers instead of typing full replies, Bitmoji is honestly one of the quickest ways to do that.

Pros

  • Makes conversations more expressive
  • Works well across popular messaging apps
  • Quick sticker access without switching apps

Download: iPhone | Android

Cons

  • Not ideal as a full-time keyboard replacement
  • Requires Bitmoji setup

Key Features to Look for in a Keyboard App

Before you download any keyboard, it helps to know what actually matters.

  • Predictive text and autocorrect: The best keyboards predict your next word and fix mistakes without turning your sentence into something else.
  • Swipe and voice typing: Swipe typing should be fast and accurate. Voice typing should work well even when you are outdoors or multitasking.
  • Emoji, GIFs, and stickers: A good keyboard makes it easy to express emotion quickly without digging through multiple menus.
  • Clipboard and text shortcuts: If you paste OTPs, addresses, links, or repeated text often, clipboard history and shortcuts can save time every single day.
  • Accessibility features: Look for adjustable key size, haptic feedback, and easy cursor movement. These features make typing more comfortable in the long term.
  • Privacy controls: Always check which permissions the keyboard requests, especially on iPhone, where “Full Access” changes what the keyboard can do.

Choose the Right Keyboard App…

These are the best keyboards you can use on iPhone and Android phones, as determined by rigorous testing. But if you are still confused about which keyboard on this list suits your needs, let me make it easy for you.

  • If you want the simplest recommendation, Gboard is the best overall keyboard for most people.
  • If you want smarter predictions and faster chat replies, SwiftKey is excellent.
  • If you write formal content and care about clean writing, keep the Grammarly Keyboard installed.
  • If privacy matters most, Typewise is the strongest choice.
  • If your focus is expressive texting, Bitmoji Keyboard is the most fun add-on.

Remember that no matter which keyboard you choose, it can access what you type. Therefore, always review permissions and avoid suspicious apps with unclear privacy policies.

Which keyboard do you use on your phone right now, and what do you wish it did better? Drop your thoughts in the comments.

FAQs

Are third-party keyboard apps safe to use on iPhone and Android?

Yes, as long as you download trusted keyboards from reputable developers and review permissions. Avoid unknown theme keyboards that request unnecessary access.

Which keyboard app is best for privacy?

Typewise is one of the best privacy-focused keyboard options, especially if you want a clean experience without excessive tracking.

Which keyboard app has the best autocorrect and predictions?

For most users, Gboard delivers the best balance of autocorrect and predictions, while SwiftKey is excellent for predictive learning over time.

What is the best keyboard app for multiple languages on iPhone and Android?

Both Gboard and SwiftKey handle multilingual typing very well, especially if you often switch languages mid-sentence.

title.rendered: iPhone Notifications Not Working? Causes and Fixes That Work

content.rendered:
Notifications are a big part of the iPhone experience. They help you stay updated with messages, calls, emails, app alerts, reminders, and more. So when notifications are delayed or not popping up, it can feel frustrating and confusing. 

In this complete guide, you’ll learn why iPhone notifications might not be working and step-by-step solutions to fix them. Whether notifications aren’t showing at all, are arriving late, or are only failing for certain apps, this guide will help you resolve the issue with ease. 

Table of Contents
  • Common Symptoms of iOS Notification Issues
  • Why Notifications Are Not Showing on My iPhone
  • Basic Checks Before Deep Troubleshooting
    • Check Volume Settings and Ensure iPhone Is Not on Silent Mode
    • Confirm Stable Internet Connection
    • Connected Apple Watch or iPhone Mirroring
  • Check Notification Settings on iPhone
  • Restart iPhone
  • Fix Notifications Not Working for Specific Apps
    • Enable In-App Notifications Settings
  • Turn Off Focus Mode and Do Not Disturb
  • Enable Background App Refresh
  • Check Low Power Mode
  • Update iOS to the Latest Version
  • Fix Notification Issues After iOS Update
  • Advanced Fixes (Last Resort)
    • Reset Network Settings
    • Restore iPhone Using Backup
  • When to Contact Apple Support
  • Final Thoughts

Common Symptoms of iOS Notification Issues 

iPhone notifications keep you connected in real time. So, when it stops popping up, you might miss urgent calls, work messages, or critical app alerts.

You may be facing a notification problem if: 

  • Notifications are not showing on the Lock Screen 
  • Alerts appear late or only when you open the app 
  • Sounds or vibrations don’t work 
  • Notifications work for some apps but not others 
  • Notifications stopped working after an iOS update 

Why Notifications Are Not Showing on My iPhone 

You get two types of alerts on your iPhone. First is the push notifications, which are sent from app servers (like messaging or social media apps) and require an internet connection.

Next is the local notifications, such as reminders or alarms, that do not always need internet access. If either type fails, notifications may stop appearing. 

Common reasons include: 

  • Silent mode or Focus Mode is enabled
  • Notifications are turned off for specific apps 
  • Low Power Mode is restricting background activity 
  • Screen Time restrictions are blocking alerts 
  • iOS bugs or outdated software 
  • App-level notification settings are disabled 

Basic Checks Before Deep Troubleshooting 

Before changing advanced settings or resetting anything, it’s important to start with basic checks. Many notification issues happen because of small, easy-to-miss settings. These quick checks solve the problem for a large number of users.

Check Volume Settings and Ensure iPhone Is Not on Silent Mode 

If the iPhone notification sound is not working, it might be because of the active Silent mode.

  1. Go to Settings > Sounds & Haptics and drag the Ringtone and Alerts slider to ensure Silent mode is off.
  2. Tap Haptics and select Always Play.

While at it, you can change the alert tone. Choose the one you can easily identify.

Confirm Stable Internet Connection 

Most notifications, especially from messaging, email, and social apps, require an active internet connection.

Check the following:

  • Open Control Center and ensure Wi-Fi or Mobile Data is turned on.
  • Try opening a website or app to confirm the connection is working.
  • Switch between Wi-Fi and Mobile Data to rule out network-specific issues.

For mobile data:

  1. Go to Settings > Cellular.
  2. Scroll down and tap Show All.
  3. Ensure the affected apps are allowed to use mobile data.

Connected Apple Watch or iPhone Mirroring 

If you use an Apple Watch, notifications may appear on the watch instead of your phone, especially when it’s locked.

To test this:

  • Unlock the iPhone and see if notifications appear there.
  • Temporarily disable Bluetooth or power off the Apple Watch.

This can also happen if your Mac is connected to your iPhone.

  1. Click the Apple menu on your Mac and select System Settings.
  2. Choose Notifications in the sidebar and click Allow notifications from iPhone.
  3. Toggle off Allow notifications from iPhone and check if alerts are popping up on your phone.

Check Notification Settings on iPhone 

If basic checks look fine, the next step is to review notification settings on the iPhone itself. iOS gives you app-level control, and a single disabled option can prevent notifications from appearing or making a sound.

  1. Open Settings > Notifications.
  2. Check that Show Previews is set to Always.
  3. Set the Display As option on Stack or List.
  4. Scroll down and select the affected app.
  5. Toggle on Allow Notifications.
  6. Then verify these options:
    • Alerts are enabled (Lock Screen, Notification Center, or Banners).
    • Sounds are turned on.
    • Badges are enabled if you rely on app icons for alerts.
    • Time Sensitive Notifications (if available) are allowed.

If notifications work for some apps but not others, the issue is almost always found here.

Tip: If Scheduled Summary is enabled, notifications may arrive at set times instead of instantly. If you want to receive them in real-time, simply turn it off. 

Restart iPhone 

Temporary system glitches can prevent notifications from working. Restarting your iPhone refreshes system processes and often fixes minor bugs. 

  1. Press and hold the Side and Volume buttons until you see the power off option.
  2. Drag the slider to switch off your iPhone.
  3. Wait a few seconds, then press the Side button to power it on.

Fix Notifications Not Working for Specific Apps 

Sometimes notifications work fine on your iPhone, but one or two apps don’t send alerts at all. This usually means the issue is with that specific app, not the whole system.

The first solution is to re-enable notifications for those individual apps from Settings. You may follow the above steps for this. Refreshing the app’s notification permission often fixes the issue instantly.

Enable In-App Notifications Settings

Most third-party apps have their own notification controls inside the app, separate from iPhone settings.

  1. Navigate to Settings > Notifications and select the affected app.
  2. Scroll down and tap [App name] Notifications Settings at the bottom.
  3. It will redirect you to the app’s settings.
  4. Make sure alerts, sounds, and message notifications are enabled.

If in-app notifications are turned off, your iPhone cannot show alerts, even if system settings are correct.

Turn Off Focus Mode and Do Not Disturb 

Focus Mode can silence or hide notifications from selected apps or contacts, making it seem like notifications are not working. 

To turn it off:

  1. Swipe down Control Center and check if the Focus tile is showing any focus mode name.
  2. Tap the tile to open Focus lists and select the focus name to turn it off.
  3. Next, go to Settings > Focus.
  4. Check Schedules or Smart Activation.
  5. Turn them off if you don’t want automatic activation.

Many users don’t realize Focus Mode is scheduled, which causes repeated notification issues.

Tip

If you want to keep Focus Mode on, add important apps to Allowed Apps and key contacts to Allowed People.

Enable Background App Refresh 

Without background refresh, apps cannot:

  • Fetch new data and check for new messages
  • Sync new content
  • Trigger timely notifications

This often causes “notifications only show when I open the app” issues.

To enable it:

  1. Go to Settings > General > Background App Refresh.
  2. Tap Background App Refresh.
  3. Select Wi-Fi & Cellular Data. 
  4. Get back and check that each app is enabled.

Check Low Power Mode 

Low Power Mode saves battery by:

  • Reducing background activity
  • Limiting app refresh
  • Delaying notifications

This can make alerts arrive late or not at all.

To turn off Low Power Mode safely: 

  1. Open Settings and go to Battery.
  2. Scroll down and toggle off Low Power Mode. 
  3. Your battery will drain faster, but notifications will work normally again.
Note

Use Low Power Mode only when the battery is low and disable it once charging is available. 

Update iOS to the Latest Version 

Older iOS versions may contain bugs that interfere with notifications, especially after app updates.

  1. Go to Settings > General > Software Update.
  2. Tap Update Now to install any available updates. 

If the iPhone update fails, ensure enough storage space, a stable internet, and sufficient battery before retrying. 

Fix Notification Issues After iOS Update 

Notification problems often appear right after an iOS update. This usually happens because system settings are reindexed, background services restart, or app permissions don’t migrate perfectly to the new version.

If the issue affects only specific apps, reinstalling them can help.

  1. Tap and hold the app on your home screen and select Remove App. Confirm your choice by tapping Delete App.
  2. Now, restart your iPhone to remove all temporary data.
  3. Then open the App Store and download the app again.
  4. Once it is reinstalled, go to Settings > Apps and select the app.
  5. Allow Notifications and Background App Refresh.

This refreshes app permissions and clears corrupted app-level notification data caused by the update.

Advanced Fixes (Last Resort) 

Use these methods only if all previous steps fail, as they reset important system data or settings.

Reset Network Settings 

Notification delivery is heavily dependent on network services. Resetting network settings can resolve hidden connectivity issues.

  1. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  2. Tap on Reset > Reset Network Settings.
  3. Enter your passcode and confirm your decision.

It will delete your Wi-Fi networks and passwords, VPN settings, and cellular and APN configurations. Don’t worry; your data and apps will remain untouched.

Restore iPhone Using Backup 

If the notification problems persist with multiple apps and settings, a full restore may be necessary.

Best approach:

  1. Back up your iPhone using iCloud or a computer.
  2. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  3. Tap Erase All Content and Settings.
  4. Restore from your backup during setup.

This removes deeply rooted system bugs introduced during the iOS update.

When to Contact Apple Support 

If none of the above fixes work, the problem may be tied to a deeper system or hardware issue.

You should contact Apple Support if you notice:

  • Notifications fail even after a full restore
  • No sound or vibration across the entire system
  • Other system features malfunction (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, Face ID)
  • The issue persists across multiple iOS versions

All of the above symptoms may indicate faulty or corrupted firmware or hardware. Have your iOS version, affected apps, and troubleshooting steps ready to speed up the process. 

Final Thoughts

Notifications not working on iPhone can be annoying, but most issues are easy to fix with the right steps. From checking basic settings to applying advanced fixes, this guide covers everything you need clearly and simply. 

Follow each section carefully, and in most cases, your notifications will be back to normal in no time. If the problem persists, don’t hesitate to contact Apple Support for expert assistance. 

FAQs

Why are my notifications not working on iPhone but only for one app?

This usually happens due to app-specific notification settings. Go to Settings > Notifications > [App Name] and make sure Allow Notifications, alert styles, sounds, and background app refresh are enabled. Also, check in-app notification settings and confirm the app is allowed to use mobile data or Wi-Fi.

Why do iPhone notifications show up late?

Late notifications are commonly caused by poor internet connection, Low Power Mode, Background App Refresh being disabled, or Notification Summary grouping alerts for later delivery. Turning them off often restores real-time alerts.

How do I fix iPhone notifications not showing on the Lock Screen?

Open Settings > Notifications > [App Name] and ensure Lock Screen alerts are enabled. Also, check Show Previews (set to Always) and confirm no Focus mode is hiding Lock Screen notifications.

Why are notifications going to my Apple Watch but not my iPhone?

When an Apple Watch is connected, notifications are designed to appear on the watch instead of the iPhone, especially when the phone is locked. Unlock the iPhone to receive alerts on it, or temporarily turn off Bluetooth or power down the Apple Watch to test notification behavior.

mainEntity.name: Why are my notifications not working on iPhone but only for one app?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually happens due to app-specific notification settings. Go to Settings > Notifications > [App Name] and make sure Allow Notifications, alert styles, sounds, and background app refresh are enabled. Also, check in-app notification settings and confirm the app is allowed to use mobile data or Wi-Fi.

mainEntity.name: Why do iPhone notifications show up late?

acceptedAnswer.text: Late notifications are commonly caused by poor internet connection, Low Power Mode, Background App Refresh being disabled, or Notification Summary grouping alerts for later delivery. Turning them off often restores real-time alerts.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix iPhone notifications not showing on the Lock Screen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Settings > Notifications > [App Name] and ensure Lock Screen alerts are enabled. Also, check Show Previews (set to Always) and confirm no Focus mode is hiding Lock Screen notifications.

mainEntity.name: Why are notifications going to my Apple Watch but not my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: When an Apple Watch is connected, notifications are designed to appear on the watch instead of the iPhone, especially when the phone is locked. Unlock the iPhone to receive alerts on it, or temporarily turn off Bluetooth or power down the Apple Watch to test notification behavior.

keyPoints.title: Check Notification Settings
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure notifications are allowed for specific apps and within app settings, including enabling banners, sounds, and lock screen notifications.

keyPoints.title: Enable Notification Center on Lock Screen
keyPoints.explanation: Make sure Notification Center is turned on in Settings face ID & Passcode to see notifications on your lock screen.

keyPoints.title: Restart and Verify Focus Mode**
keyPoints.explanation: Restart your iPhone to fix temporary glitches, and confirm that Focus Mode is turned off, as it can mute notifications.

keyPoints.title: Update iPhone Software Regularly
keyPoints.explanation: Always keep your iPhone updated to the latest iOS version, as software updates fix bugs and improve notification reliability.
